2156: void pathland_qt_layer_apply(const PathlandQtCommand *cmds, uint32_t count) {
2157:     if (!g.initialized || !cmds || count == 0) {
2158:         return;
2159:     }
2160:     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
2161:         const PathlandQtCommand &c = cmds[i];
2162:         switch (c.kind) {
2163:         case PLQT_CREATE_NODE: {
2164:             const uint16_t component = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
2165:             QQuickItem *item = createComponent(g.engine, g.root, qmlFor(component, c.a).toUtf8());
2166:             if (item) {
2167:                 g.widgets[c.a] = item;
2168:                 g.components[c.a] = component;
2169:                 if (component == PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
2170:                     const uint32_t id = c.a;
2171:                     QObject::connect(item, &QQuickItem::widthChanged, item,
2172:                                      [id, item]() { reportFit(id, item->width()); });
2173:                 }
2174:                 if (isTextInput(component)) {
2175:                     const uint32_t id = c.a;
2176:                     QObject::connect(item, &QQuickItem::activeFocusChanged, item, [id, item]() {
2177:                         const bool focused = item->hasActiveFocus();
2178:                         if (focused) {
2179:                             g.focused_id = id;
2180:                             g.focused_component = g.components[id];
2181:                         } else if (g.focused_id == id) {
2182:                             g.focused_id = 0;
2183:                             g.focused_component = 0;
2184:                         }
2185:                         if (g.bridge) {
2186:                             g.bridge->focusChanged(id, focused);
2187:                             g.bridge->editingChanged(id, focused);
2188:                         }
2189:                     });
2190:                 }
2191:             }
2192:             break;
2193:         }
2194:         case PLQT_DELETE_NODE:
2195:             deleteNode(c.a);
2196:             break;
2197:         case PLQT_INSERT_CHILD:
2198:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c);
2199:             break;
2200:         case PLQT_REMOVE_CHILD: {
2201:             const uint32_t parentId = c.a;
2202:             const uint32_t childId = c.b;
2203:             g.parents.erase(childId);
2204:             auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
2205:             siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
2206:             if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
2207:                 rebuildPickerModel(parentId);
2208:             } else if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
2209:                 reconcileNav(parentId);
2210:             } else {
2211:                 QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
2212:                 if (child) {
2213:                     child->setParentItem(nullptr); // keep alive (may be reinserted)
2214:                 }
2215:             }
2216:             break;
2217:         }
2218:         case PLQT_MOVE_CHILD:
2219:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c); // reorder == reinsert at index
2220:             break;
2221:         case PLQT_SET_TEXT: {
2222:             QQuickItem *item = findWidget(c.a);
2223:             if (item && c.str) {
2224:                 g.suppress = true;
2225:                 item->setProperty("text", QString::fromUtf8(c.str, static_cast<int>(c.str_len)));
2226:                 g.suppress = false;
2227:             }
2228:             // A picker option's label feeds its parent's ComboBox model.
2229:             auto pit = g.parents.find(c.a);
2230:             if (pit != g.parents.end() && g.components[pit->second] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
2231:                 rebuildPickerModel(pit->second);
2232:             }
2233:             // Record for the test hook.
2234:             if (c.str && c.str_len > 0) {
2235:                 const uint32_t n = c.str_len < sizeof(g.last_text) - 1 ? c.str_len
2236:                                                                        : sizeof(g.last_text) - 1;
2237:                 std::memcpy(g.last_text, c.str, n);
2238:                 g.last_text[n] = '\0';
2239:                 g.last_text_len = n;
2240:             }
2241:             break;
2242:         }
2243:         case PLQT_SET_PROPERTY: {
2244:             const uint16_t prop = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
2245:             const uint8_t vt = static_cast<uint8_t>((c.b >> 16) & 0xFF);
2246:             g.suppress = true;
2247:             applyProperty(c.a, prop, vt, c.c);
2248:             g.suppress = false;
2249:             break;
2250:         }
2251:         case PLQT_SET_STRING_PROPERTY:
2252:             g.suppress = true;
2253:             applyStringProperty(c.a, static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b), c.str, c.str_len);
2254:             g.suppress = false;
2255:             break;
2256:         case PLQT_RESET_NODE:
2257:             resetNode(c.a);
2258:             break;
2259:         case PLQT_SET_SCHEME:
2260:             break; // MVP: scheme handling is a follow-up
2261:         case PLQT_SET_DATE: {
2262:             // A DATE_PICKER value: days since the Unix epoch + millis of day.
2263:             // The renderer owns the formatting (QML approximation of a picker).
2264:             if (QQuickItem *item = findWidget(c.a)) {
2265:                 const qint64 days = static_cast<int32_t>(c.b);
2266:                 const QDate date = QDate(1970, 1, 1).addDays(days);
2267:                 QString text = date.toString(QStringLiteral("yyyy-MM-dd"));
2268:                 const int millis = static_cast<int>(c.c);
2269:                 if (millis > 0) {
2270:                     const int hours = millis / 3'600'000;
2271:                     const int minutes = (millis / 60'000) % 60;
2272:                     text += QStringLiteral(" %1:%2")
2273:                                 .arg(hours, 2, 10, QChar('0'))
2274:                                 .arg(minutes, 2, 10, QChar('0'));
2275:                 }
2276:                 g.suppress = true;
2277:                 item->setProperty("text", text);
2278:                 g.suppress = false;
2279:             }
2280:             break;
2281:         }
2282:         }
2283:     }
2284:     g.apply_count += count;
2285: }

1: //! # pathland-render-qt
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **Qt Quick renderer**. It consumes opcode frames (via
4: //! `pathland_render_core::RenderTree`) and maps them **incrementally** onto a
5: //! Qt Quick scene graph — `Row`/`Column` for stacks, `Text` for text, Qt Quick
6: //! Controls for buttons/fields/sliders.
7: //!
8: //! The crate is split across languages on purpose:
9: //! - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), the
10: //!   sent-state **delta diff** ([`renderer::QtRenderer`]), the `Pump`
11: //!   transport seam, wire encoding, and the C ABI for foreign hosts
12: //!   ([`capi`]).
13: //! - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell and maps the delta
14: //!   command batch onto QML items. It reports inputs back through a wake
15: //!   callback; the renderer **never drains events** — the host drains its own
16: //!   ring, symmetric with frames flowing in.
17: //!
18: //! The Qt layer is the only place that touches Qt; the protocol core
19: //! (`pathland-core`/`pathland-view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.

1: //! C ABI for the Pathland Qt renderer (foreign hosts, e.g. Java via JNA).
2: //!
3: //! Mirrors `pathland-render-gtk`'s `capi.rs`:
4: //! - `pathland_qt_run(host, on_event)` — pump a `pathland-view-native`
5: //!   `NativeHost`'s ring in-process.
6: //! - `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` — pump a
7: //!   `libpathland_core` ring borrowed in-process (the route for hosts that
8: //!   emit opcodes themselves, e.g. the Java DSL's `RingOpcodeSink`).
9: //!
10: //! Both block until the Qt event loop exits and pass a bare program name to
11: //! Qt (the process argv belongs to the embedding host — e.g. a JVM's `-cp` /
12: //! `-D` flags — and must not be parsed as Qt options).
13: 
14: use std::ffi::{c_char, c_void, CStr};
15: 
16: use pathland_core::Event;
17: use pathland_core_transport::{
18:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
19: };
20: use pathland_native::NativeHost;
21: 
22: use crate::run::{run_with_pump_sized, EventCallback, Pump};
23: 
24: /// A `Pump` over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost` owned by the foreign host.
25: struct NativeHostHandle(*mut NativeHost);
26: 
27: impl Pump for NativeHostHandle {
28:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
29:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); the host must not destroy
30:         // the host until `pathland_qt_run` returns.
31:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }
32:     }
33: 
34:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
35:         // SAFETY: as above.
36:         unsafe { DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *self.0, event) }
37:     }
38: }
39: 
40: /// A `Pump` over a `libpathland_core` `RingTransport` borrowed from the foreign
41: /// host. Same contract as [`NativeHostHandle`].
42: struct CoreRingHandle(*mut RingTransport);
43: 
44: impl Pump for CoreRingHandle {
45:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
46:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); the ring outlives the call.
47:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }
48:     }
49: 
50:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
51:         // SAFETY: as above.
52:         unsafe { DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *self.0, event) }
53:     }
54: }
55: 
56: /// Run the Qt renderer over a `pathland-view-native` host's shared ring.
57: ///
58: /// `host` is the opaque handle from `pathland_native_create`; the renderer
59: /// pumps its ring in-process (frames in, events out). `on_event` is called
60: /// (on the Qt main thread, with no payload) whenever a raw input was written;
61: /// the host then drains the event ring via `pathland_native_drain_events` and
62: /// may re-enter `pathland_native_*` to update the tree and re-emit.
63: ///
64: /// Blocks until the Qt event loop exits (window closed).
65: #[no_mangle]
66: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_qt_run(host: *mut c_void, on_event: Option<EventCallback>) {
67:     if host.is_null() {
68:         return;
69:     }
70:     let pump: Box<dyn Pump> = Box::new(NativeHostHandle(host as *mut NativeHost));
71:     run_with_pump_sized("Pathland Qt Demo", pump, on_event, 420, 220);
72: }
73: 
74: /// Run the Qt renderer over a `libpathland_core` ring borrowed in-process.
75: ///
76: /// `ring` is the pointer from `pathland_core_ring_mut` (the underlying
77: /// `RingTransport` of a `pathland_core_create` handle). This is the route for
78: /// hosts that emit opcodes themselves — no `pathland-view-native` host is
79: /// involved. `width`/`height` size the default window (0 = renderer default).
80: /// Blocks until the Qt event loop exits.
81: #[no_mangle]
82: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_qt_run_ring(
83:     ring: *mut c_void,
84:     on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
85:     width: u32,
86:     height: u32,
87: ) {
88:     if ring.is_null() {
89:         return;
90:     }
91:     let pump: Box<dyn Pump> = Box::new(CoreRingHandle(ring as *mut RingTransport));
92:     run_with_pump_sized(
93:         "Pathland Qt Demo",
94:         pump,
95:         on_event,
96:         width.max(1) as i32,
97:         height.max(1) as i32,
98:     );
99: }
100: 
101: /// Set the local asset root so web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media sources
102: /// resolve against a directory extracted by the host (mirrors
103: /// `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`). Call before `pathland_qt_run*`.
104: #[no_mangle]
105: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir: *const c_char) {
106:     if dir.is_null() {
107:         crate::ffi::pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root(std::ptr::null());
108:         return;
109:     }
110:     let root = CStr::from_ptr(dir).to_string_lossy().into_owned();
111:     let c = std::ffi::CString::new(root).unwrap_or_default();
112:     crate::ffi::pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root(c.as_ptr());
113: }

## Plan: HStack/VStack layout tests for the Qt renderer

### What I found

The Qt renderer is split: Rust (`renderer.rs` delta diff + `ffi.rs` FFI boundary) → C++ (`qt_layer.cpp` QML scene). VStack renders as a wrapper `Item` holding a `ColumnLayout`; HStack holds a `RowLayout`. Existing live-scene tests (`fill_child_stretches_inside_stack`, `default_stack_stretch_and_spacer`, `renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`) already assert fill/preferred/spacing wiring, but **none assert actual child geometry** — i.e. that VStack children stack vertically and HStack children flow horizontally.

The C++ test hooks already expose `pathland_qt_layer_widget_size` (width/height) and `pathland_qt_layer_render_once` (force a synchronous layout pass), but **there is no position (x/y) hook**, so "laid out correctly" can't yet be asserted.

### Changes

**1. Add a position test hook** (needed to assert geometry):
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/qt_layer.cpp` — add `pathland_qt_layer_widget_position(uint32_t id, uint32_t which)` returning `item->x()` (which==0) / `item->y()` (which==1), next to `pathland_qt_layer_widget_size`.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/pathland_qt.h` — declare it.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/ffi.rs` — add the matching `extern "C"` declaration.

**2. Add two tests** in `ffi.rs` `mod tests` (using the existing `with_qt` harness + `pathland_qt_layer_render_once`, hand-built command batches like `fill_child_stretches_inside_stack`, with fixed main-axis sizes for deterministic geometry):

- `vstack_lays_out_children_vertically` — VSTACK(1) with two TEXT children (fixed `HEIGHT`=50) + `SPACING`=10:
  - `y(2) == 0`, `y(3) ≈ y(2) + h(2) + 10` (second child below the first)
  - `x(2) == x(3)` (default cross-axis stretch aligns left)
  - gap ≈ spacing (assert with a small epsilon, e.g. 0.5)
- `hstack_lays_out_children_horizontally` — HSTACK(1) with two TEXT children (fixed `WIDTH`=100) + `SPACING`=10:
  - `x(2) == 0`, `x(3) ≈ x(2) + w(2) + 10` (second child to the right)
  - `y(2) == y(3)` (default cross-axis stretch aligns top)
  - gap ≈ spacing

**3. Update `status.md`** — add the two tests to the "Verified by" list.

**4. Verify** — `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (needs Qt6 dev libs; runs offscreen).

### Notes / assumptions
- I'll use hand-built `Command` batches (matching the existing layout tests) rather than the DSL for precise, deterministic geometry. I can add a DSL-driven end-to-end variant too if you'd prefer the tests exercise the full DSL→engine→frame→renderer path.
- Root stacks are anchored to fill the 420×220 window; `render_once()` forces the Qt Quick Layouts pass so `x()`/`y()`/`width()`/`height()` are populated before asserting.

Want me to proceed with hand-built commands only, or also add a DSL end-to-end test for each?

519: ### ZStack — `ZSTACK` 0x12
520: 
521: Depth-overlapping layer stack: children are drawn in depth order — **child index =
522: draw order**, later = on top. An explicit `Z_INDEX` overrides that order: a
523: higher value draws **on top of** lower values, and equal values tie-break by
524: child index (SwiftUI `.zIndex(_:)` parity). **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (enum:
525: `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), plus layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill
526: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, `PADDING`, `CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset). **No `SPACING`** —
527: children occupy the same box by design; there is no gap between them.
528: 
529: **Layout & sizing** (SwiftUI `ZStack` / Compose `Box` semantics)
530: 
531: - **Overlay allocation**: unlike a flex stack, children do **not** add to each
532:   other along an axis — they share one box. Each child keeps its own size (a
533:   Fixed box, or a Hug natural size) and is **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` on
534:   **both axes**; only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's size.
535: - **Own size**: the stack **hugs to its largest child** by default — on each
536:   axis its size is the **maximum** of its children's sizes, never the sum. A
537:   Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
538:   propagation (a `Fill` child on an axis makes the Hug stack `Fill` on that
539:   axis, see the stack layout model above) — expands to the parent's proposal.

I've researched the ZStack implementation and spec. Here's my plan.

## Plan: ZStack layout test for the Qt renderer

### Findings
- In the Qt renderer, `ZSTACK` (`0x12`) maps to a **plain QML `Item`** (`qt_layer.cpp:431`) — not a `RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout` like VStack/HStack.
- Its children attach **directly** to that `Item` (`insertChild` only reroutes to an inner layout for `isStackComponent`, which ZStack is *not*), so they overlap at the same origin instead of being distributed along an axis.
- This matches spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack default: no `SPACING`, children share one box, `ALIGNMENT` default `0` = top-leading, each child keeps its own size.
- No new test hook is needed — `pathland_qt_layer_widget_position`, `_widget_size`, and `_widget_child_count` (added for the VStack/HStack tests) cover everything. This is purely additive Rust.

### Change
Add one test `zstack_overlaps_children_in_depth` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/ffi.rs` (`mod tests`), right after `hstack_lays_out_children_horizontally`, mirroring the hand-built command style:

- Build: `ZSTACK` (id 1) as root (`insert_child(0, 1)`), two `TEXT` children (id 2 "A", id 3 "B"), each with fixed `WIDTH`=100 / `HEIGHT`=50.
- `render_once` to force the layout pass.
- Assert:
  - `widget_child_count(1) == 2` — children are direct children of the ZStack (no inner axis layout).
  - `position(2) == position(3) == (0,0)` — both children overlap at the top-leading origin (depth stacking, not VStack/HStack axis flow).
  - `size(2) == 100×50` (and same for 3) — each child keeps its own box rather than being stretched or summed.

### Note / optional
The spec also specifies draw order (child index = on-top; `Z_INDEX` override), but the Qt renderer doesn't yet manage z-order explicitly (children just inherit Qt's default stacking). Verifying that would require a new "topmost child" test hook. I'm **not** including it unless you want it — let me know.

### Verify
`cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (full suite stays green, +1 test).

I've researched the Qt renderer's IMAGE support. Here's my plan.

## Plan: IMAGE test for the Qt renderer

### Findings
- `IMAGE` (`0x02`) maps to a QML `Image { objectName: "pl%1"; fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectFit }` (`qt_layer.cpp:459`).
- `IMAGE_SOURCE` (`0x1002`, a `STRING` property) → `item->setProperty("source", resolveAsset(value, asset_root))` (`qt_layer.cpp:1693`).
- `CONTENT_MODE` (`0x001C`, `F32`) → `fillMode` = `PreserveAspectCrop` (2) when value ≥ 0.5, else `PreserveAspectFit` (1) (`qt_layer.cpp:1569`).
- No dedicated image test exists today. The existing `pathland_qt_layer_widget_prop_text(id, prop, …)` hook reads any QML property as a string — sufficient for `source` and `fillMode`, so **no new C++/FFI hook is needed**.

### Change
Add one test `image_sets_source_and_content_mode` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/ffi.rs` (`mod tests`), hand-built commands (consistent with the VStack/HStack/ZStack/text tests):

- Create `IMAGE` (id 1) as root child (`insert_child(0, 1)`).
- `Command::set_string_property(1, property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE, "/tmp/image.png")`.
- `render_once` (not strictly needed for property reads, but keeps parity with other layout tests — I'll skip it actually, since these are property-only assertions).
- Assert:
  - `source` property == `"/tmp/image.png"` (round-trips through `resolveAsset` unchanged for a non-`/_pathland/` path).
  - default `fillMode` == `"1"` (`PreserveAspectFit`).
  - after `Command::set_property(1, property_id::CONTENT_MODE, value_type::F32, 1.0f32.to_bits())`, `fillMode` == `"2"` (`PreserveAspectCrop`).
- Add a small `str_prop(id, prop) -> String` helper (sibling to the existing `read_text` / `int_prop`) to read `source`.

### Optional extra (let me know)
Also verify the asset-root resolution: call `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root("/assets")`, set `IMAGE_SOURCE` to `"/_pathland/img.png"`, and assert `source` resolves to `"/assets/img.png"`. This tests the web-style asset path used by the desktop demos.

### Verify
`cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (full suite stays green, +1 test). Update `status.md` "Verified by".

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the Pathland demo scripts. Source this file; it defines
# $ROOT (the repository root) and the prerequisite-build helpers each demo uses.

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Build the Rust HTML renderer cdylib (embedded in the Java pathland-render-html jar).
build_rust_html() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-render-html)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the desktop demos link: the core ring (libpathland_core)
# and the GTK4 renderer (libpathland_gtk).
build_gtk_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the Qt desktop demo links: the core ring
# (libpathland_core) and the Qt Quick renderer (libpathland_qt).

  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt)

content.text:
## Diagnosis (root cause)

The split layout is broken by `RESET_NODE`, not by the HStack/sidebar structure itself.

The Rust diff (`renderer.rs::diff`) emits, for **every node that has properties**, a `RESET_NODE` command immediately before re-sending that node's full property set (first render included). Order in a frame is:

1. `CREATE_NODE`
2. `INSERT_CHILD` (this is where the structural fill defaults are applied)
3. `RESET_NODE` + `SET_PROPERTY` for each node

The structural fill is applied in `insertChild` (`qt_layer.cpp:1910–1951`):
- **default cross-axis stretch** (sidebar gets `Layout.fillHeight` as an HStack child),
- **Spacer** main-axis fill,
- **ScrollView / SIZE_THAT_FITS** greedy fill.

But `resetNode` (`qt_layer.cpp:1746–1764`) then does:

```cpp
const auto kids = lay->childItems();
for (QQuickItem *k : kids)
  if (QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(k))
    a->setFillWidth(false); a->setFillHeight(false);
    a->setPreferredWidth(-1); a->setPreferredHeight(-1);
```

i.e. it clears the **children's** fill flags, and nothing re-applies the structural stretch. So on the first frame:

- The sidebar loses `fillHeight` → a `RowLayout` centers a non-filling child vertically (the exact "sidebar vertically centered" symptom).
- The `ScrollView` loses its `fillWidth`/`fillHeight` (and the nav content inside collapses to the top-left).

This is why my earlier hand-built layout tests passed (they call `pathland_qt_layer_apply` directly and never emit `RESET_NODE`), while the DSL-driven demo (which goes through the real diff) is broken.

## Plan

**1. Extract the structural fill into a helper** in `qt_layer.cpp`, e.g. `applyChildLayoutFill(parentId, childId, child, attach)`, containing exactly the three blocks currently at `1911–1951` (default cross-axis stretch, Spacer expansion, ScrollView/SIZE_THAT_FITS greedy fill). Replace the inline blocks in `insertChild` with a call to it.

**2. Re-apply it after reset** in `resetNode`: inside the existing `if (QQuickItem *lay = layoutOf(item))` block, after the fill-flag reset loop, iterate the node's children and call `applyChildLayoutFill(id, childId, child, lay)`. This keeps the reset's intended behavior (clearing stale fills for *removed* `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` FILL properties) while restoring the renderer-owned structural stretch that has no backing property.

**3. Add a regression test** (`ffi.rs`, DSL-driven through `Harness` + `QtRenderer::apply_frame` so `RESET_NODE` is actually emitted) mirroring the split layout:

- `hstack![ vstack![...].modifiers(Frame::width(200.0)), text("content").modifiers(Frame::width(f32::INFINITY)) ]` as the root.
- `render_once`, then assert:
  - sidebar (`VStack`) has `y == 0` and `height == window height` (stretched, not centered),
  - the content child has `x == 200` (right of the sidebar, not overlapping the sidebar area).

**4. Update `status.md`** (mention the RESET_NODE/stretch fix + the regression test).

**5. Verify**: `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (the new test should fail before the fix, pass after), and rebuild the demo dylibs.

### Out of scope (noted, not fixed now)
- Changing a child's `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` from FILL → fixed leaves a stale fill flag (the reset is parent-scoped, not self-scoped). Pre-existing, unrelated to this split-layout regression.

One question before I proceed: the sidebar uses a fixed `width(200)` and the cross-axis stretch is unconditional (it overrides a child's own fixed cross size). Should I keep that existing behavior, or make the default stretch skip children that set their own cross-axis size (closer to CSS `align-items: stretch`)? I'd keep existing behavior to stay focused — let me know if you want the stricter version.
What does the spec say regarding the cross axis stretch?

57: 
58: ## Container allocation rules
59: 
60: Containers (`VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`ZSTACK`, `GRID`, `SCROLLVIEW`, and the semantic
61: composites) allocate their children by these rules. The **main axis** is the
62: container's layout direction; the **cross axis** is the other one.
63: 
64: ### Main axis
65: 
66: A child's main-axis size comes from its size kind:
67: 
68: - **Fixed** → the child is allocated exactly its box.
69: - **Fill** → the child expands; **leftover main-axis space goes only to `Fill`
70:   children** (shared between them). A container with no `Fill` child leaves the
71:   leftover space empty at the end of its main axis.
72: - **Hug** (or absent) → the child's natural size, positioned at the start of
73:   the leftover space.
74: 
75: ### Cross axis
76: 
77: - A **Fixed** or **Hug** child keeps its own size on the cross axis and is
78:   **positioned** by the container's `ALIGNMENT`.
79: - **`ALIGNMENT` positions but never resizes.** It selects the placement of
80:   Fixed/Hug children within leftover space; it does not stretch them. The value
81:   is a **2D position code** (the [ZStack table](./PRIMITIVES.md#zstack--zstack-0x12)):
82:   a stack reads a single axis (a `VStack` the horizontal component, an `HStack`
83:   the vertical — codes `0/1/2`), a `ZStack`/grid both axes. With no `ALIGNMENT`
84:   (code `0`/absent) the default cross-axis position is the **start**. Code `3`
85:   is `top-center`, never a stretch; stretching lives in the **child's size
86:   kind** (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` = `FILL`).
87: - Only a **`Fill`-sized child** fills the container's cross size.
88: - **The default is *hug*, not stretch.** A child with no cross-axis size is NOT
89:   stretched to fill the cross axis. This deliberately matches **SwiftUI**
90:   (children report their ideal size; a `VStack`/`HStack` aligns them) and
91:   **Compose** (Row/Column children wrap content cross-axis unless
92:   `fillMaxWidth/Height`), rather than CSS flexbox's `align-items: stretch`
93:   default. A renderer must therefore NOT stretch cross-axis children implicitly
94:   (e.g. the web renderer uses `align-items: flex-start`, not the flex default).
95: 
96: ### Layout-greedy primitives
97: 
98: The cross-axis hug default has **four intrinsic exceptions** — primitives whose
99: native behavior is to fill space (SwiftUI/Compose precedent), so an app does not
100: need an explicit `FILL` frame to get their natural behavior:
101: 
102: | Primitive | Greedy on | Precedent |
103: |-----------|-----------|-----------|
104: | `DIVIDER` | cross-axis | SwiftUI `Divider()` fills the stack's available width/height; CSS `hr` is block-width |
105: | `SCROLLVIEW` | both axes | SwiftUI `ScrollView` / Compose scroll fills the available space (the point of a scroll region) |
106: | `COLOR` | both axes | SwiftUI `Color` is layout-greedy and expands unless a frame constrains it |
107: | `SPACER` | main-axis | `Spacer()` absorbs leftover main-axis space by definition |
108: 
109: Rules:
110: 
111: - Greedy fills **only the axis the primitive is designed to fill** — never both
112:   for `DIVIDER`/`SPACER`.
113: - An **explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` always overrides** the greedy default (`Fixed`
114:   = that box; `FILL` = stretch anyway).
115: - Every other primitive (Text, Image, stacks, buttons, controls) is a plain
116:   **Fixed / Fill / Hug** node governed by the size model — no implicit
117:   greediness.
118: 
119: ### Non-visual nodes (layout-transparent)
120: 
121: Some nodes exist in the retained tree but render **no** element and take part in
122: **no** layout. They are **layout-transparent**:
123: 
124: - They are **not slots**: a stack/grid parent MUST NOT allocate space to them and
125:   MUST NOT contribute spacing for them (they are skipped entirely, as if absent).
126: - They have no box, no intrinsic size, and no content mode; `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` and
127:   alignment do not apply.
128: - Their position in the tree carries **no layout meaning** — applications place
129:   them for lifetime stability, not for geometry.
130: 
131: | Node | Role |
132: |------|------|
133: | `COMMENT` 0x7F | Opaque/debug marker |
134: | `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30 | Owns a media resource + transport; referenced by a `VIDEO` surface ([MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md)) |

435: 
436: **Main vs cross axis.** The **main axis** is the stack's layout direction
437: (VStack = vertical, HStack = horizontal); the other is the **cross axis**.
438: 
439: **Main-axis allocation.** A child is Fixed (exact box), Fill (expands), or Hug
440: (natural). **Leftover main-axis space goes only to `Fill` children** (and to
441: `Spacer`, which is Fill by nature); a stack with no Fill child leaves the
442: leftover empty at the end. Every other child is packed from the start.
443: 
444: **Cross-axis allocation.** A child keeps its own size on the cross axis and is
445: **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` — position-only, it never resizes. A stack reads a
446: **single axis** of the 2D position code (see the [ZStack alignment
447: table](#zstack--zstack-0x12)): a `VStack` reads the horizontal component
448: (`0/1/2` = leading/center/trailing), an `HStack` the vertical (`0/1/2` =
449: top/center/bottom). The default is the start position (Compose `Column` defaults
450: `Alignment.Start`, `Row` defaults `Alignment.Top`; SwiftUI's stack default is
451: `.center` — a per-framework difference, all three are expressible with an
452: explicit `ALIGNMENT`). Only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's
453: cross size.
454: 
455: **Fill propagation.** A Hug-sized stack that contains a **`Fill`-sized child or
456: `Spacer` on an axis is itself `Fill`-sized on that axis** — the child's
457: expansion propagates to the stack, which then fills its parent's proposal on
458: that axis. This matches both reference frameworks:
459: 
460: - SwiftUI `VStack { Button().frame(maxWidth: .infinity) }` fills the width.
461: - Compose `Column { Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) }` fills the width.
462: - `VStack { Spacer() }` fills the proposed height.
463: 
464: A full-width row is therefore expressed as a `Fill`-width child (or `Spacer`)
465: inside the stack, never by stretching the stack itself.
466: 
467: **Spacing.** `SPACING` is a fixed gap between **adjacent** children (never
468: before the first or after the last), clamped to ≥ 0. It matches SwiftUI
469: `VStack(spacing:)` and Compose `Arrangement.spacedBy(...)`. Leftover space is
470: distributed by `Fill` children / `Spacer`, never by the gap.
471: 
472: **Insets.** `CONTENT_MARGINS` is the stack's uniform content inset
473: (equivalently, `PADDING` on the stack). Both compose; when both are present on
474: the same node, precedence is per-edge `PADDING_*` > `PADDING` >
475: `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
476: 
477: **Overflow.** A Fixed box **constrains layout but does not clip**: content that
478: exceeds the box is drawn outside it unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it (SwiftUI
479: `.clipped()` parity). A stack inside a `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls instead.
480: 
481: ### VStack — `VSTACK` 0x10
482: 
483: Vertical flex stack. **Properties**: `SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT` (enum: `Leading`=0,
484: `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
485: 
486: **Layout & sizing**
487: 
488: - **Main axis (vertical)**: children are allocated per the stack model —
489:   Fixed exact, Fill expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A
490:   Hug VStack's height is the sum of its children's heights plus `SPACING`
491:   between them.
492: - **Cross axis (horizontal)**: children keep their own width (a Fixed box, or a
493:   Hug natural width); `Fill`-width children stretch to the stack's width. Narrow
494:   children are positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default Leading/Start).
495: - **Own size**: Hug by default (height = content + spacing; width = widest
496:   child). A Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
497:   propagation — expands to the parent's proposal. A `Fill`-width child makes
498:   the stack full-width; a `Fill`-height child makes it full-height.
499: - **Edge cases**: negative `SPACING` → 0; no Fill child + leftover → empty at
500:   the end; a Fixed-width child narrower than the stack keeps its exact box and
501:   is aligned; a `Fill` child in a Hug stack propagates (fills the parent's
502:   proposal); root stacks are typically `Fill`
503:   (`.modifiers(frame(f -> f.width(FILL).height(FILL)))`).
504: 
505: ### HStack — `HSTACK` 0x11
506: 
507: Horizontal flex stack. Same properties as `VStack`, mirrored:
508: 
509: - **Main axis (horizontal)**: children per the stack model — Fixed exact, Fill
510:   expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A Hug HStack's width
511:   is the sum of its children's widths plus `SPACING`.
512: - **Cross axis (vertical)**: children keep their own height (Fixed or Hug);
513:   `Fill`-height children stretch. Positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default
514:   Leading/Start; Compose `Row` defaults to `Top`, SwiftUI's HStack to `.center`).

168: #### Constraint properties for native layout
169: 
170: The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
171: native layout properties (e.g. `SPACING` → a gap between children,
172: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` → size requests). Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL
173: (expand to available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT (native intrinsic size).
174: 
175: > **Allocation semantics** — the exact meaning of a Fixed / `FILL` / `HUG_CONTENT`
176: > size, how containers distribute space to children (main axis: only `FILL`
177: > expands; cross axis: children hug unless `FILL`), and how content fits inside
178: > a Fixed box, are defined in [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md).
179: 
180: > **Units — logical points.** All size properties (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`SPACING`/
181: > `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS`, …) are expressed in an abstract **logical point**
182: > unit — the same abstraction as SwiftUI points, Jetpack Compose `dp`, and CSS
183: > pixels. A renderer MUST allocate the requested points box and fit content
184: > within it; it must never treat the value as a device-pixel size. Each renderer
185: > maps points to its native unit and resolves its own device resolution (logical
186: > points × scale factor), so the same value yields the same physical size across
187: > renderers.
188: 
189: | Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
190: |----------|-------|------|----------------|
191: | `SPACING` | `0x0001` | F32 | Gap between children |
192: | `ALIGNMENT` | `0x0002` | F32 (enum code) | Cross-axis position (never stretches; default = Leading, `Fill`(3) = default hug — see LAYOUT.md) |
193: | `CONTENT_MARGINS` | `0x0005` | F32 | Uniform inset between a stack's edge and its content |
194: | `WIDTH` | `0x100B` | F32 | Width hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
195: | `HEIGHT` | `0x100C` | F32 | Height hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
196: | `GRID_COLUMNS` | `0x001E` | F32 | Grid column count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit; a count, never a pixel width — see PRIMITIVES.md §Grid) |
197: | `GRID_ROWS` | `0x001F` | F32 | Grid row count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit) |
198: | `GRID_TRACKS` | `0x0020` | STRING | Per-track grid spec (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>`, comma-separated) — takes precedence over the counts |
199: 
200: #### Text properties
201: 
202: Text-bearing nodes (`TEXT`, `BUTTON` labels, `TEXT_FIELD`) carry their content
203: via `SET_TEXT` (0x03) and their layout via these properties:
204: 
205: | Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
206: |----------|-------|------|----------------|
207: | `TEXT` | `0x000A` | STRING | The text content (a `SET_TEXT`-style arena string) |

86: /// The size hint a node carries on `axis`.
87: fn axis_hint(node: &HostNode, axis: Axis) -> SizeHint {
88:     size_hint(node.properties.get(&axis.property()).copied())
89: }
90: 
91: /// A layout-greedy primitive that fills the main axis (`main_axis` = true) or
92: /// the cross axis (false) by nature (LAYOUT.md): `SPACER` fills the main axis,
93: /// `DIVIDER` the cross axis, `COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW` both.
94: fn greedy_fills(node: &HostNode, main_axis: bool) -> bool {
95:     match node.component_type {
96:         component_type::SPACER => main_axis,
97:         component_type::DIVIDER => !main_axis,
98:         component_type::COLOR | component_type::SCROLLVIEW => true,
99:         _ => false,
100:     }
101: }
102: 
103: /// Whether a node is **effectively `FILL`-sized on `axis`** — it is `FILL`
104: /// itself, a layout-greedy primitive that fills `axis` by nature, or (fill
105: /// propagation) a Hug-sized container whose subtree carries a `FILL`-sized
106: /// child / greedy filler on `axis`. A Fixed box bounds its subtree, so a
107: /// Fixed-sized container never propagates (its children fill within the box).
108: ///
109: /// `resolve` maps a child id to its node; pass a no-op resolver when the caller
110: /// has no tree (then only the node's own size kind / greediness is considered).
111: pub fn effective_fill(node: &HostNode, axis: Axis, main_axis: bool, tree: &RenderTree) -> bool {
112:     match axis_hint(node, axis) {
113:         SizeHint::Fill => return true,
114:         SizeHint::Fixed(_) => return false,
115:         SizeHint::None => {}
116:     }
117:     if greedy_fills(node, main_axis) {
118:         return true;
119:     }
120:     if !propagates_fill(node.component_type) {
121:         return false;
122:     }
123:     // A child's greedy nature is relative to its own parent (`node`): a child's
124:     // main axis is `axis` iff `node` is a stack whose main axis is `axis`.
125:     let child_main = stack_orientation(node.component_type)
126:         .map(|o| Axis::of(o) == axis)
127:         .unwrap_or(false);
128:     node.children
129:         .iter()
130:         .any(|&cid| tree.node(cid).is_some_and(|c| effective_fill(c, axis, child_main, tree)))
131: }
132: 
133: /// Containers that hug their content and therefore propagate a `FILL` child up
134: /// (SwiftUI/Compose parity): stacks and the ZStack. `GRID`/`SCROLLVIEW` are
135: /// excluded — a grid sizes its cells, a scroll view is greedy already.
136: fn propagates_fill(component_type: u16) -> bool {
137:     matches!(
138:         component_type,
139:         component_type::VSTACK
140:             | component_type::HSTACK
141:             | component_type::ZSTACK
142:             | component_type::LAZY_VSTACK
143:             | component_type::LAZY_HSTACK
144:             | component_type::PROXY_VIEW
145:     )
146: }

148: /// The stack's explicit cross-axis `ALIGNMENT` position. `Fill` (3) and absent

The spec is unambiguous, and it's the opposite of what the Qt renderer currently does.

## What the spec says

**Cross-axis default is *hug*, never stretch** — and this is stated as a hard renderer obligation:

> "Only a **`Fill`-sized child** fills the container's cross size." … "**The default is *hug*, not stretch.** A child with no cross-axis size is NOT stretched to fill the cross axis. This deliberately matches **SwiftUI** … and **Compose** … rather than CSS flexbox's `align-items: stretch` default. A renderer must therefore NOT stretch cross-axis children implicitly (e.g. the web renderer uses `align-items: flex-start`, not the flex default)."
> — `spec/LAYOUT.md:87-94`

Reinforced in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md:444-453` (cross-axis: "children keep their own size … positioned by `ALIGNMENT` — position-only, it never resizes … Only a `Fill`-sized child stretches") and `spec/OPCODE.md:192` (`ALIGNMENT`: "Cross-axis position (never stretches … `Fill`(3) = default hug)").

So the rules are:

1. **Cross-axis: hug by default, positioned at start.** `ALIGNMENT` only positions; `Fill(3)` is just the default hug (same as absent), *not* a stretch.
2. **Stretch is expressed only via the child's size kind** (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT = FILL`), never via alignment.
3. **"Effectively FILL"** is what stretches, and it's three things:
   - explicit `FILL` size,
   - a **layout-greedy primitive** — `SPACER` (main axis), `DIVIDER` (cross), `COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW` (both) (`spec/LAYOUT.md:96-117`),
   - **fill propagation** — a Hug stack/ZStack/proxy whose subtree contains a FILL child or greedy filler on an axis is itself FILL on that axis (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md:455-465`).

## What this means for the bug

- The Qt renderer's `insertChild` "default cross-axis stretch" (`qt_layer.cpp:1911-1922`, sets `fillWidth`/`fillHeight` on every child when no `ALIGNMENT`) **is a spec violation** — it implements CSS `align-items: stretch`, which LAYOUT.md explicitly forbids.
- The **GTK and HTML renderers already implement the correct model** (GTK: `layout.rs::effective_fill`/`cross_axis_align`, defaulting to `Start`; HTML: `align-items: flex-start`). Qt is the outlier.
- The sidebar is *supposed* to stretch — not because of CSS stretch, but via **fill propagation**: it's a `VStack` containing a `Spacer`, so `effective_fill(sidebar, vertical)` is true, and an HStack stretches an effectively-FILL child on its cross axis. The `Sidebar.java` comment ("align-items: stretch") is phrased in CSS terms and is technically wrong, but the *result* it wants is spec-correct via the Spacer's fill propagation.

So the correct fix is not "keep the stretch and re-apply it after reset" (my earlier suggestion) — it's to **replace the Qt renderer's CSS-style default stretch with the spec's hug-not-stretch + effective-fill model** (mirroring the GTK renderer), and separately ensure RESET_NODE doesn't wipe the resulting fills.

Want me to revise the plan around that: (a) remove the implicit cross-axis stretch, (b) implement `effective_fill` (explicit FILL + greedy primitives + fill propagation) for stack cross-axis alignment, (c) fix the RESET_NODE clearing so greedy/structural fills survive, and (d) add spec-conformance tests (including a split-layout regression that asserts the sidebar stretches via its Spacer)? I can also flag the greedy-primitive gaps (`DIVIDER`/`COLOR`) if you want them in the same pass or separate.
yes to all

I've completed the research. Here's the finalized plan.

## Goal

Bring the Qt renderer's stack cross-axis behavior into line with the spec (`spec/LAYOUT.md` "Cross axis" + "Layout-greedy primitives", `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` stack model, `spec/OPCODE.md` `ALIGNMENT`), mirroring what the GTK (`layout.rs::effective_fill`/`main_axis_align`/`cross_axis_align`) and HTML (`align-items: flex-start`) renderers already do.

The model to implement:
- **Cross axis defaults to hug**, positioned at start; `ALIGNMENT` only positions (`Fill(3)` ≡ absent ≡ hug, never stretch).
- A child stretches only if it is **effectively FILL** on that axis:
  1. explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT = FILL`,
  2. a **greedy primitive** (`SPACER` main, `DIVIDER` cross, `COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW` both; `SIZE_THAT_FITS` both),
  3. **fill propagation** — a Hug `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`ZSTACK`/lazy/proxy whose subtree has a FILL child/greedy filler on that axis is itself FILL on that axis (a Fixed box bounds its subtree → no propagation).
- **Main axis**: leftover space goes only to effectively-FILL children + `SPACER`.

This also resolves the reported split-layout bug: the sidebar (`VStack` containing a `Spacer`) becomes effectively-FILL on the vertical axis via propagation, so as an HStack child it stretches top-to-bottom — and the `RESET_NODE` fill-clearing bug disappears because fills are recomputed at end-of-frame.

## Changes — `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`

1. **Track size hints** (new state on `LayerState g`): `std::unordered_map<uint32_t, uint8_t> width_hint, height_hint` (enum `None/Fill/Fixed`). Populate in `applySize` (FILL→Fill, positive finite→Fixed, HUG/absent→None); erase in `resetNode` (props are re-sent after RESET) and `deleteNode`.

2. **Add the spec model helpers** (mirroring GTK `layout.rs`):
   - `greedy_fills(component, main_axis)`: `SPACER`→main, `DIVIDER`→!main, `COLOR|SCROLLVIEW|SIZE_THAT_FITS`→both.
   - `propagates_fill(component)`: `VSTACK|HSTACK|ZSTACK|LAZY_VSTACK|LAZY_HSTACK|PROXY_VIEW` (composite controls too — see below).
   - `effective_fill(id, axis, main_axis)`: hint Fill→true / Fixed→false / None→greedy→true; else if propagates, recurse `children_of` with `child_main = (node's orientation main axis == axis)`; guard missing/non-visual nodes → false.

3. **Replace `applyStackAlignment`** with `applyChildAxes(parentId, childId, child)` that, for a stack child, sets:
   - **main-axis** fill iff `effective_fill(child, main, true)`, else clears it;
   - **cross-axis** fill iff `effective_fill(child, cross, false)`, else clears fill and sets `Layout.alignment` from `stack_align[parentId]` (start/center/end; `Fill(3)`/absent → start).
   - Remove the old `idx==3 → setFill` branch (that was the CSS-stretch violation).

4. **Remove the inline structural-fill blocks from `insertChild`** (default cross-axis stretch ~1911–1922, Spacer ~1923–1933, ScrollView/SIZE_THAT_FITS ~1934–1951, and the `applyStackAlignment(parentId, child)` call ~1910). Keep attach, root-anchor, foreground inheritance, and the SIZE_THAT_FITS "selected child fills the slot" special case.

5. **Add `recomputeLayout()`** (call at the end of `pathland_qt_layer_apply`, after the command loop): iterate every `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy/`PROXY_VIEW`/composite container id in `g.components`, skip `nav_slots` and non-visual children, and for each `children_of` child call `applyChildAxes`. This is O(n) per frame, idempotent, and makes `RESET_NODE`'s fill-clearing harmless.

6. **Simplify** `applyProperty` `ALIGNMENT` to just `g.stack_align[id] = value` (drop `reapplyStackAlignment`; the recompute pass applies it). Keep `resetNode` mostly as-is but add the two hint erases.

## Test changes — `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/ffi.rs`

Rewrite the two tests that encoded the old CSS-stretch behavior:
- `default_stack_stretch_and_spacer` → `default_cross_axis_hugs_and_spacer_expands`: HStack TEXT child (no size) now asserts `widget_fill(…, height) == 0` (hug); keep Spacer-main-fill and explicit-ALIGNMENT assertions.
- `fill_child_stretches_inside_stack` → keep the explicit `WIDTH=FILL`→`fillWidth` / fixed→`preferredWidth` / root-anchor assertions; change the `ALIGNMENT=Fill(3)` cross-stretch assertions to hug (`fill == 0`).

Add spec-conformance tests (hand-built commands, plus one DSL-driven for the reset path):
- `cross_axis_hugs_by_default` (HStack/VStack child with no size → no cross fill).
- `explicit_fill_stretches_cross_axis` (HEIGHT=FILL in HStack, WIDTH=FILL in VStack → fill set).
- `greedy_primitives_fill_by_nature` (DIVIDER cross, COLOR both, SPACER main).
- `fill_propagation_stretches_sidebar` — DSL → engine → `QtRenderer::apply_frame` (so `RESET_NODE` is emitted) mirroring `SplitNavDemo`: HStack root → VStack sidebar (fixed `Frame::width(200)` + a `Spacer` child) + a content child; `render_once` then assert sidebar `y==0`/`height==window height` and content `x==200`.

Existing VStack/HStack/ZStack/text/image geometry tests remain valid (they assert ordering/alignment/origin, not implicit stretch).

## Docs

- `status.md`: replace the "default cross-axis stretch (CSS align-items:stretch)" wording with the spec model (hug + effective-fill + propagation + greedy primitives), and note the corrected tests + the split-layout regression.

## Verify

- `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (Qt6 offscreen) — new tests should fail before the fix, pass after; full suite green.
- Rebuild the demo dylibs (`cargo build -p pathland-render-qt -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt-demo`) and optionally run `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` / `scripts/run-rust-qt-demo.sh` for a visual check.

## Out of scope / noted

- Changing a child's own `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` from FILL→fixed leaves a stale fill flag (parent-scoped reset). The recompute pass now re-derives fills each frame, so this becomes a non-issue; I won't add separate self-scoped reset logic.

content.text:
Implemented and verified. The Qt renderer now follows the spec's cross-axis model instead of CSS stretch.

**Renderer (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`)**
- Added per-node `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` size-kind tracking (`width_hint`/`height_hint`) and the spec model: `greedyFills`, `propagatesFill`, `stackOrientation`, `effectiveFill` (explicit FILL + greedy primitives + fill propagation, incl. composite bodies), and `applyChildAxes` (main-axis fill + cross-axis hug/stretch + `ALIGNMENT` positioning with `Fill(3)` = start).
- Removed the old CSS-style default cross-axis stretch and the insert-time Spacer/ScrollView fill blocks.
- Added `recomputeLayout()` at the end of each frame batch (skips promoted nav slots/non-visual), so `RESET_NODE`'s style reset can no longer wipe the structural fills — the original split-layout bug.
- `applySize` records hints; `resetNode`/`deleteNode`/`reset`/`shutdown` clear them; `ALIGNMENT` is now applied by the recompute pass.

**Tests (`src/ffi.rs`)** — 47 passing
- Rewrote `explicit_width_inside_stack_and_cross_axis_hugs` and `default_cross_axis_hugs_and_spacer_expands` to the hug default.
- Added `explicit_fill_stretches_cross_axis`, `greedy_primitives_fill_by_nature` (DIVIDER/COLOR/SPACER axes), `composite_button_body_propagates_fill` (menu rows stay full width), and the DSL-driven `fill_propagation_stretches_sidebar` regression (through `apply_frame`, so `RESET_NODE` is exercised): sidebar `y=0`, full window height, content at `x≈200`.

**Docs**: `status.md` + `todo.md` updated to describe hug + effective-fill + propagation.

**Build**: `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` → **47 passed, 0 failed**; demo dylibs/binary rebuilt (`libpathland_qt.dylib`, `pathland-render-qt-demo`, `libpathland_core.dylib`). The Java Qt demo picks up the fresh dylib at runtime (no Java changes).

## Plan: switch the Java Qt demo to `MusicPlayerView`

The "demo" here is the **Java Qt demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`), which currently mounts `SplitNavDemo`. `MusicPlayerView` is a shared `dev.pathland.demo.music` view already used by the GTK demo, and the Qt renderer already implements everything it needs (non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` + `AudioOutput`, `IMAGE` album art, `SIZE_THAT_FITS`, `MEDIA_*` events). Two gaps in the Qt demo must be closed to run it.

### Changes (all under `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo/` unless noted)

1. **`src/main/java/dev/pathland/demo/qt/QtHost.java`**
   - Import `dev.pathland.demo.music.MusicPlayerView` instead of `dev.pathland.demo.SplitNavDemo`.
   - Remove `import dev.pathland.view.Platform;` and `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.environmentBinding;`.
   - Seed `activePath = Signals.signal("/")` (placeholder — `MusicPlayerView` has no router; keep the `InputDispatcher(result, activePath)` wiring as-is).
   - Mount: `emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), new Environment(state));` (drop the `environmentBinding(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)` modifier).
   - Update the class Javadoc to describe the music player + app-driven media (mirror `GtkHost`).
   - Optionally bump `WINDOW_WIDTH/HEIGHT` from `1100×720` → `1180×800` for GTK parity. (Current width is already > the player's `1024` wide-fit threshold, so the Now-Playing sidebar shows either way.)

2. **`src/main/java/dev/pathland/demo/qt/RingEventReader.java`**
   - Add the 4 missing media decode cases (mirror the GTK reader):
     `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED`, `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED`, `MEDIA_ENDED`, `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` → `Event.media*`.

3. **`src/test/java/dev/pathland/demo/qt/RingEventReaderTest.java`**
   - Add `decodesMediaEvents()` (mirror the GTK test) to cover the new cases.

4. **`pom.xml`** — update the `<description>` ("SplitNavDemo … native navigation" → music player).

5. **Doc touch-ups** (minor, keeps things accurate):
   - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md` (the "Java JNA demo … mounts `SplitNavDemo`" lines) → music player.
   - `AGENTS.md` (lines ~169 and ~181 referencing the Java Qt demo's `SplitNavDemo`) → music player.
   - `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` header comment → music player.

### Verify
- `cd lib/java && mvn -pl pathland-qt-demo -am install` (compiles + runs `RingEventReaderTest`).
- Rebuild dylibs if needed (already current; media support is in `libpathland_qt.dylib`).
- `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` to smoke-test; audio playback depends on QtMultimedia mp3 support (AVFoundation on macOS).

### Notes / assumptions
- I'm assuming "the demo" = the **Java Qt demo** (the one with `SplitNavDemo`), not the Rust `pathland-render-qt-demo` (a counter/slider demo with no Java music view). Confirm if you meant something else.
- The Qt renderer's nav adapter (`SplitNavDemo`) stays in place — still exercised by the renderer's tests.

2: //! retained renderer, and hands the C++ shell a tick callback so the ring is
3: //! pumped on the Qt main thread between frames — the Qt analogue of the GTK
4: //! renderer's glib idle pump.
5: //!
6: //! Contract (mirrors `pathland-render-gtk`):
7: //! - The renderer **never drains events** — it writes `EVENT` opcodes via
8: //!   `Pump::send_input` and wakes the host; the host drains its own ring.
9: //! - All access is on the Qt main thread; the host re-enters the ring from the
10: //!   wake callback on the same thread (the ring is the decoupling buffer, so a
11: //!   control signal firing during frame apply needs no deferred flush).
12: 
13: use std::cell::RefCell;
14: use std::ffi::c_void;
15: use std::ffi::CString;
16: use std::rc::Rc;
17: 
18: use pathland_core::tokens::Scheme;
19: use pathland_core::{category, meta, Event};
20: use pathland_core_transport::{
21:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
22: };
23: 
24: use crate::ffi::{ev, QtEvent};
25: use crate::renderer::QtRenderer;
26: 
27: /// The bidirectional transport surface the renderer pumps: frames in
28: /// (guest → host) and events out (host → guest).
29: pub trait Pump {
30:     /// Read the next guest → host frame.
31:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;
32:     /// Write a host → guest raw input as an `EVENT` opcode.
33:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
34: }
35: 
36: impl Pump for RingTransport {
37:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
38:         FrameSource::next_frame(self)
39:     }
40:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
41:         DriverTransport::send_input(self, event)
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: /// A host-supplied event callback, invoked (with no payload) when the renderer
46: /// has written a raw input into the host → guest event ring. The host drains
47: /// the ring itself.
48: pub type EventCallback = extern "C" fn();
49: 
50: /// What to do with a Qt raw input.
51: enum QtAction {
52:     /// Encode + write into the event ring, then wake the host.
53:     Send(Event),
54:     /// A platform color-scheme change: re-resolve tokens in the renderer
55:     /// (no host wake — the re-apply flows back as `SET_PROPERTY` commands).
56:     Scheme(Scheme),
57:     None,
58: }
59: 
60: /// Decode a `QtEvent` (C++ → Rust) into an action.
61: fn decode_event(raw: &QtEvent) -> QtAction {
62:     match raw.kind {
63:         ev::POINTER_DOWN => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerDown {
64:             target: raw.node_id,
65:             x: raw.x,
66:             y: raw.y,
67:             secondary: false,
68:         }),
69:         ev::POINTER_MOVE => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerMove {
70:             target: raw.node_id,
71:             x: raw.x,
72:             y: raw.y,
73:             hovering: false,
74:             leaving: false,
75:         }),
76:         ev::POINTER_UP => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerUp {
77:             target: raw.node_id,
78:             x: raw.x,
79:             y: raw.y,
80:             secondary: false,
81:         }),
82:         ev::VALUE_CHANGED => QtAction::Send(Event::ValueChanged {
83:             target: raw.node_id,
84:             value: raw.value,
85:         }),
86:         ev::TEXT_CHANGED => {
87:             // The string is length-prefixed, not guaranteed NUL-terminated.
88:             let slice =
89:                 unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(raw.str_ as *const u8, raw.str_len as usize) };
90:             QtAction::Send(Event::TextChanged {
91:                 target: raw.node_id,
92:                 value: String::from_utf8_lossy(slice).into_owned(),
93:             })
94:         }
95:         ev::NAVIGATE_BACK => QtAction::Send(Event::Navigate { url: None }),
96:         // Media transport reports target the MEDIA_CONTROLLER (spec/MEDIA.md).
97:         ev::MEDIA_PLAY_STATE => QtAction::Send(Event::MediaPlayStateChanged {
98:             target: raw.node_id,
99:             playing: raw.value >= 0.5,
100:         }),
101:         ev::MEDIA_TIME => QtAction::Send(Event::MediaTimeUpdated {
102:             target: raw.node_id,
103:             seconds: raw.value,
104:         }),
105:         ev::MEDIA_ENDED => QtAction::Send(Event::MediaEnded {
106:             target: raw.node_id,
107:         }),
108:         ev::MEDIA_VOLUME => QtAction::Send(Event::MediaVolumeChanged {
109:             target: raw.node_id,
110:             volume: raw.value,
111:         }),
112:         ev::MEDIA_DURATION => QtAction::Send(Event::MediaDurationChanged {
113:             target: raw.node_id,
114:             seconds: raw.value,
115:         }),
116:         ev::FIT_CHANGED => QtAction::Send(Event::FitChanged {
117:             target: raw.node_id,
118:             index: raw.value,
119:         }),
120:         ev::POINTER_ENTER => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerMove {
121:             target: raw.node_id,
122:             x: 0.0,
123:             y: 0.0,
124:             hovering: true,
125:             leaving: false,
126:         }),
127:         ev::POINTER_LEAVE => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerMove {
128:             target: raw.node_id,
129:             x: 0.0,
130:             y: 0.0,
131:             hovering: false,
132:             leaving: true,
133:         }),
134:         ev::KEY_DOWN => QtAction::Send(Event::KeyDown {
135:             target: raw.node_id,
136:             key_code: raw.key_code,
137:             modifiers: raw.modifiers,
138:             repeat: raw.repeat != 0,
139:         }),
140:         ev::KEY_UP => QtAction::Send(Event::KeyUp {
141:             target: raw.node_id,
142:             key_code: raw.key_code,
143:             modifiers: raw.modifiers,
144:         }),
145:         ev::FOCUS => QtAction::Send(Event::FocusChanged {
146:             target: raw.node_id,
147:             focused: raw.value >= 0.5,
148:         }),
149:         ev::EDITING => QtAction::Send(Event::EditingChanged {
150:             target: raw.node_id,
151:             editing: raw.value >= 0.5,
152:         }),
153:         ev::SUBMIT => QtAction::Send(Event::Submit {
154:             target: raw.node_id,
155:         }),
156:         ev::SCHEME_CHANGED => QtAction::Scheme(if raw.value >= 0.5 {
157:             Scheme::Dark
158:         } else {
159:             Scheme::Light
160:         }),
161:         _ => QtAction::None,
162:     }
163: }

165: /// Whether a frame carries `META::RESET` (clear all output).
166: fn frame_has_reset(frame: &pathland_core::Frame<'_>) -> bool {
167:     frame
168:         .opcodes()
169:         .any(|op| op.category() == category::META && op.command() == meta::RESET)
170: }

172: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
173: // C-ABI path: a boxed `Pump` over an opaque host/ring pointer (capi.rs).
174: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
175: 
176: /// The per-run state held on the stack of [`run_with_pump_sized`]; the C++
177: /// shell receives an opaque pointer to it.
178: struct Runner {
179:     pump: Box<dyn Pump>,
180:     renderer: QtRenderer,
181:     on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
182: }
183: 
184: /// Pump one tick: flush the next pending frame into the renderer.
185: fn pump_once(runner: &mut Runner) {
186:     match runner.pump.next_frame() {
187:         Ok(Some(batch)) => {
188:             let frame = batch.frame();
189:             if frame_has_reset(frame) {
190:                 runner.renderer.reset();
191:             } else {
192:                 runner.renderer.apply_frame(frame);
193:             }
194:         }
195:         Ok(None) => {}
196:         Err(_) => {}
197:     }
198: }
199: 
200: /// Qt timer tick → Rust pump (the C++ shell calls this with the `Runner` ptr).
201: pub extern "C" fn qt_tick(user: *mut c_void) {
202:     if user.is_null() {
203:         return;
204:     }
205:     // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); `Runner` outlives `run`.
206:     let runner = unsafe { &mut *(user as *mut Runner) };
207:     pump_once(runner);
208: }
209: 
210: /// Qt wake (a control reported an input) → host callback. The renderer does
211: /// not decode the event; it only wakes the host, which drains its own ring.
212: pub extern "C" fn qt_wake(user: *mut c_void) {
213:     if user.is_null() {
214:         return;
215:     }
216:     // SAFETY: as above.
217:     let runner = unsafe { &*(user as *const Runner) };
218:     if let Some(cb) = runner.on_event {
219:         cb();
220:     }
221: }
222: 
223: /// Qt raw input (C++ → Rust): encode the `Event`, write it into the ring, then
224: /// wake the host. The host drains its own ring — the renderer never drains.
225: /// A scheme change instead re-resolves tokens in the renderer (no host wake).
226: pub extern "C" fn qt_event(ev: *const QtEvent, user: *mut c_void) {
227:     if ev.is_null() || user.is_null() {
228:         return;
229:     }
230:     // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); `ev` is valid for the call.
231:     let raw = unsafe { &*ev };
232:     let runner = unsafe { &mut *(user as *mut Runner) };
233: 
234:     match decode_event(raw) {
235:         QtAction::Send(event) => {
236:             if let Err(e) = runner.pump.send_input(&event) {
237:                 eprintln!("pathland-render-qt: send_input failed: {e:?}");
238:             }
239:             if let Some(cb) = runner.on_event {
240:                 cb();
241:             }
242:         }
243:         QtAction::Scheme(scheme) => runner.renderer.set_scheme(scheme),
244:         QtAction::None => {}
245:     }
246: }
247: 
248: /// Run the Qt renderer over any `Pump`, blocking until the Qt event loop exits.
249: pub fn run_with_pump_sized(
250:     title: &str,
251:     pump: Box<dyn Pump>,
252:     on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
253:     width: i32,
254:     height: i32,
255: ) {
256:     let mut runner = Runner {
257:         pump,
258:         renderer: QtRenderer::new(),
259:         on_event,
260:     };
261:     let user = &mut runner as *mut Runner as *mut c_void;
262:     let title = CString::new(title).unwrap_or_else(|_| CString::new("Pathland").unwrap());
263:     // Blocks until the window closes (Qt main loop exits).
264:     unsafe {
265:         crate::ffi::pathland_qt_layer_run(
266:             title.as_ptr(),
267:             width,
268:             height,
269:             qt_wake,
270:             qt_tick,
271:             qt_event,
272:             user,
273:         );
274:     }
275: }

277: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
278: // Rust-demo path: a shared `Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>` + a host closure
279: // (mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`). The pump borrow is held across frame
280: // application, so the batch's zero-copy view of the shared ring stays valid.
281: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
282: 
283: /// Per-run state for the shared-ring convenience path.
284: struct RingRunner {
285:     ring: Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>,
286:     renderer: QtRenderer,
287:     on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
288: }
289: 
290: // The host's drain-and-respond closure, stored for the wake trampoline
291: // (a regular comment: `thread_local!` doesn't carry doc comments).
292: thread_local! {
293:     static RING_HOST: RefCell<Option<Box<dyn FnMut()>>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
294: }
295: 
296: fn pump_once_ring(runner: &mut RingRunner) {
297:     let guard = runner.ring.try_borrow_mut();
298:     if let Ok(mut p) = guard {
299:         if let Ok(Some(batch)) = FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *p) {
300:             let frame = batch.frame();
301:             if frame_has_reset(frame) {
302:                 runner.renderer.reset();
303:             } else {
304:                 runner.renderer.apply_frame(frame);
305:             }
306:         }
307:     }
308: }
309: 
310: extern "C" fn ring_tick(user: *mut c_void) {
311:     if user.is_null() {
312:         return;
313:     }
314:     // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); `RingRunner` outlives `run`.
315:     let runner = unsafe { &mut *(user as *mut RingRunner) };
316:     pump_once_ring(runner);
317: }
318: 
319: extern "C" fn ring_host_wake(user: *mut c_void) {
320:     if user.is_null() {
321:         return;
322:     }
323:     // SAFETY: as above.
324:     let runner = unsafe { &*(user as *const RingRunner) };
325:     if let Some(cb) = runner.on_event {
326:         cb();
327:     }
328: }
329: 
330: extern "C" fn ring_event(ev: *const QtEvent, user: *mut c_void) {
331:     if ev.is_null() || user.is_null() {
332:         return;
333:     }
334:     // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread).
335:     let raw = unsafe { &*ev };
336:     let runner = unsafe { &mut *(user as *mut RingRunner) };
337: 
338:     match decode_event(raw) {
339:         QtAction::Send(event) => {
340:             let guard = runner.ring.try_borrow_mut();
341:             if let Ok(mut p) = guard {
342:                 let _ = DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *p, &event);
343:             }
344:             if let Some(cb) = runner.on_event {
345:                 cb();
346:             }
347:         }
348:         QtAction::Scheme(scheme) => runner.renderer.set_scheme(scheme),
349:         QtAction::None => {}
350:     }
351: }
352: 
353: /// Run the Qt renderer over a shared `RingTransport`, calling `on_event` (with
354: /// the ring) whenever the renderer wrote raw inputs. Mirrors
355: /// `pathland_render_gtk::run`. Blocks until the window closes.
356: pub fn run<F>(_app_id: &str, title: &str, ring: Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event: F)
357: where
358:     F: FnMut(Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>) + 'static,
359: {
360:     // A Rust closure can't be an `extern "C" fn`; store it for the trampoline.
361:     let ring_for_host = ring.clone();
362:     RING_HOST.with(|h| {
363:         let mut cb = on_event;
364:         *h.borrow_mut() = Some(Box::new(move || cb(ring_for_host.clone())));
365:     });
366:     extern "C" fn host_trampoline() {
367:         RING_HOST.with(|h| {
368:             if let Some(cb) = h.borrow_mut().as_mut() {
369:                 cb();
370:             }
371:         });
372:     }
373: 
374:     let mut runner = RingRunner {
375:         ring,
376:         renderer: QtRenderer::new(),
377:         on_event: Some(host_trampoline),
378:     };
379:     let user = &mut runner as *mut RingRunner as *mut c_void;
380:     let title = CString::new(title).unwrap_or_else(|_| CString::new("Pathland").unwrap());
381:     unsafe {
382:         crate::ffi::pathland_qt_layer_run(
383:             title.as_ptr(),
384:             420,
385:             220,
386:             ring_host_wake,
387:             ring_tick,
388:             ring_event,
389:             user,
390:         );
391:     }
392: }

spec/PRIMITIVES.md:720:### SizeThatFits — `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17

### SizeThatFits — `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17

A **fit slot**: it shows **one child at a time — the currently selected
candidate**. In the **live (delta) form** only that child is ever transmitted:
the app owns the candidates (their views never ride the wire) and transmits the
**fit query** (`FIT_QUERY`, LIST — the candidates' `minWidth` thresholds,
ascending) plus the selected child. In a **full-snapshot emission** (the web SSR
first document), every candidate is transmitted as a child — the renderer renders
all branches and the browser selects the matching one (see the visibility
contract below) so the first paint is already correct. The renderer measures its
**own allocated width** (the slot is size-taking — it stretches to its parent's
proposal, never hugs, so it always has a well-defined width) and selects the fit
**locally**:

> **Fit rule** — the selected index is `max{ i : thresholds[i] ≤ measured
> width }` (threshold 0 candidate always qualifies — the fallback); equal
> thresholds pick the **lower index**; before the first measure the app renders
> the threshold-0 candidate (index 0). The measurement is in **logical points**,
> so the pick is identical on every renderer given the same slot width.

The renderer reports its selection back with **`FIT_CHANGED`** ([EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md))
— emitted **once after the first measure, and then only when the derived fit
index changes** (a band crossing). It never streams the raw size. The app reacts
by swapping the slot's child (a `TREE` delta pair); a selection that maps to the
already-shown view re-emits **zero** opcodes. After a **full-snapshot**
presentation (all candidates laid out), the first `FIT_CHANGED` is the signal
that collapses the slot back to the live single-selected-child form.

**Candidate identity (MUST).** The candidate **index `i`** is the candidate's
position in the **ascending `FIT_QUERY` table** (equal thresholds keep the app's
surface order). In a **full-snapshot emission** the slot's **child order MUST
equal `FIT_QUERY` order** — the child at position `i` is candidate `i`. The fit
rule, the `FIT_CHANGED` payload, and the CSS gate all use this one mapping. A
candidate declared first in the DSL but carrying a **higher** `minWidth` is
therefore **not** index 0.

**Full-snapshot visibility (MUST).** In a full-snapshot emission the renderer
MUST show **exactly one** candidate — the one at `index(w)` for the slot's own
allocated width `w` — with no JS:

- the slot's own width is the query context (each slot is measured
  independently);
- each candidate is gated behind a marker carrying its `FIT_QUERY` index;
- for every threshold `T_i` with `i ≥ 1` there is a **band** that, at
  `w ≥ T_i`, makes candidate `i` visible and **hides every candidate `j ≠ i`**;
  bands are emitted **ascending** so the highest matching band wins; no band
  exists for `T_0`;
- the per-candidate **default** (below the first band / no match) is candidate
  `0` visible, every other candidate hidden;
- **invariant**: exactly one candidate is visible at every width.

**Hydration collapse (MUST).** After the first `FIT_CHANGED` the app swaps the
slot to the live single-selected-child form (the unselected candidates leave as
`TREE` deltas) and the renderer removes the full-snapshot gating — the gate
markers, the query context, and the band rules — so no CSS gate remains; a
`FIT_CHANGED` that maps to the already-shown candidate re-emits **zero** opcodes.

The collapse is signalled by the **removal of a candidate** (a `TREE` `REMOVE_CHILD`
/`DELETE_NODE` on the slot), not by an arbitrary structural op. A **full-snapshot
emission replayed as opcodes** (e.g. `META::RESYNC`) therefore does **not** collapse
the slot: the renderer reuses its existing gate (the SSR gate markers + band rules)
and keeps showing the width-correct candidate. The app's retained tree stays in the
snapshot form until the first `FIT_CHANGED` downgrade actually removes a candidate.

The concrete web realization (CSS container + per-candidate gate wrappers +
`@container` band rules) is **renderer-owned** and described in
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`.

**Shared subtrees in a full snapshot (MUST).** When the same subtree is authored
inside more than one candidate, a full-snapshot emission materializes that subtree
**once per candidate** (each candidate renders its own retained nodes). Every copy
MUST receive a **distinct node id** — no id is reused between candidates, including
nodes with identity-stable semantics such as a media controller
([MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md)). The frame's unique-node-id invariant
([OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#frame-lifecycle)) therefore holds across the whole slot.

Semantics:
- **Properties**: `FIT_QUERY` (`0x1039`, LIST).
- **Events**: `FIT_CHANGED` (`0x13`, host → guest) — reported fit index.
- **Children**: at most one in the live form; all candidates in a
  full-snapshot emission (the web SSR's first document), in `FIT_QUERY` order.
- **Renderer statelessness**: the measured width and derived index are layout
  output, not retained application state.

### ProxyView — `PROXY_VIEW` 0x1E

A **proxy view**: a transparent container whose child subtree is served by a
**different Pathland server**. It lets one app compose views from several
servers into a single unified document. The proxying server (the app that owns
the proxy node) connects to the origin server as a Pathland **host** (client),
receives the origin's subtree, and splices it into its own stream.

- **Protocol**: a container node with **exactly one** child in the live form —
  the origin subtree's root. The origin subtree's nodes are ordinary nodes of
  the same protocol; the proxying server has **remapped their node ids** into a
  disjoint high range so they never collide with the proxying app's own ids.
- **Layout**: a **transparent passthrough** container. It imposes no spacing or
  alignment of its own; it proposes its own allocated size to its single child
  and, unless the app constrains it (`frame`/size modifiers), sizes to that
  child. Renderers render it as a plain container (a box/`div`) — there is no
  proxy-specific native element.
