### Rationale

These rules are the bugs-fixed-and-avoided model of the reference renderers:

- A **Fixed image** in a row stays its box (never scaled to content or stretched
  by a tall row).
- A **Fixed/Hug child in a `Fill` container** keeps its size; leftover space
  goes to `Fill` children (or stays empty).
- A **composite button** (e.g. a library row) sizes to its content on the main

---

## Content fitting, truncation & clipping

Content-bearing views fit their content **inside** their allocated box:

- **Media** (`IMAGE`, `VIDEO`): fitted per `CONTENT_MODE` — `Fit` (0) scales to
  contain (letterboxed), `Fill` (1) scales to cover (cropped). The box is the
  allocation, never the content's intrinsic size. A `VIDEO` surface's playback
  lives on a separate `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node; audio has no visual at all (§
  Non-visual nodes) and is controlled by the application's own views.

### Text

- **Wrapping.** An unconstrained `TEXT` lays out on a **single line at its
  natural width**. It **wraps at word boundaries only when its width is
  constrained** — a Fixed `WIDTH`, or a `LINE_LIMIT` that needs multiple lines.
  An unbreakable word wider than the box may break by character. A wrapped
  Text's natural height is its **line count × line height** (so a Hug container
  can compute its size). A Fixed `HEIGHT` constrains the box; overflow follows
  the overflow rules ([above](#a-container-that-is-itself-fixed)).
- **`LINE_LIMIT`.** A positive `LINE_LIMIT` (N) clamps the rendered text to **at
  most N lines**; any overflow beyond the last visible line is replaced by an
  ellipsis `…` at its end (**tail** truncation). `0`/absent = unlimited. It does
  not force a single line — lines are formed by wrapping at the available width
  and by explicit line breaks.
- **`TRUNCATION_MODE`.** `Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2 **positions the
  ellipsis** (at the start / middle / end of the last visible line) whenever a
  `LINE_LIMIT` clamp truncates. It applies **only when such a clamp truncates**:
  on its own it has **no observable effect** (SwiftUI-aligned) — it never forces
  a single line and never truncates by itself.

### Clipping — `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`

`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` (0x1010, U8) is a **post-layout visual clip**: the node's
content and its own painted decoration (fills, backgrounds, borders) are
clipped to its **allocated bounds box** — on **both axes**. Layout is
unaffected: the node is still allocated and positioned exactly as if unclipped;
only what is painted is clipped. `0`/absent = no clipping. A `SHAPE_KIND`

## Plan: clarify the spec, then fix the ScrollView renderer

### Part 1 — Spec clarification (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §ScrollView)

The "unbounded proposal on **both** axes" sentence contradicts full-width scroll content. The fix is to note that the existing **fill-propagation** model (already defined in the stack layout model, `PRIMITIVES.md:455` and `LAYOUT.md`) applies *inside* the scroll content, against the **viewport** as the bounded proposal — no new concept, just disambiguation.

**Proposed replacement** for the "Content." paragraph:

> **Content.** The **first child** is the content; a scroll view carries a single content subtree (typically a stack), matching SwiftUI/Compose's single-content contract. The content is measured with an **unbounded proposal** on both axes — its natural size may grow beyond the viewport (that is what scrolls). **Fill propagation still applies inside the content**: a content stack with a `Fill`-sized child (or a `Spacer`) on an axis is itself `Fill`-sized on that axis (see the stack layout model above) and fills the **viewport** — the bounded proposal — on that axis. A full-width scroll row is therefore authored as a `Fill`-width child of the content stack, never by stretching the content itself. A content with no `Fill` child keeps its natural size on that axis and may be narrower/shorter than the viewport. The **viewport** is the scroll view's allocated box; a Hug `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` — or a Hug parent proposal on an axis — sizes the viewport to the content's natural size on that axis (the viewport fits the content, so that axis does not scroll).

(Optionally add a `CONFORMANCE.md`/`LAYOUT.md` vector for "ScrollView content with a `FILL`-width child → content takes the viewport width".)

### Part 2 — ScrollView renderer fix (`qt_layer.cpp`)

Extend `reconcileScrollSize` (already wired into `recomputeLayout`) to materialize content fill against the viewport:

- Locate the content child (first non-`MEDIA_CONTROLLER` child).
- On each axis where `effectiveFill(content, axis, /*main=*/false)` is true:
  - horizontal → `content->setWidth(scroll->width())`
  - vertical → `content->setHeight(max(scroll->height(), content->implicitHeight()))` (fills when short, still scrolls when tall).
- Leave hug content (no `FILL` child) at its natural size — so the existing `scroll_view_content_is_measured_unbounded` test stays green.
- Re-derive on the ScrollView's `widthChanged`/`heightChanged` (connect at `CREATE_NODE`, same pattern as `ZSTACK`), so it materializes once the viewport is actually laid out.

This makes the `TrackRowView` `Button`'s `WIDTH=FILL` propagate up through the content `VStack` and materialize against the viewport → the library expands horizontally, and the trailing `Spacer` absorbs vertical leftover while the list still scrolls when taller.

### Part 3 — Tests (`ffi.rs`)

1. **`scroll_view_content_fill_expands_to_the_viewport`** — a 300×150 `SCROLLVIEW` whose content is a `VStack` with a `WIDTH=FILL` child → content width ≈ 300 and the FILL child fills it (this test fails today and passes after the fix).
2. **`scroll_view_content_spacer_fills_and_scrolls`** (vertical) — content `VStack` with a `Spacer` and few rows → content height ≈ viewport height; with many rows → content height > viewport (scrolls).
3. Keep `scroll_view_content_is_measured_unbounded` green (hug content unchanged).

### Part 4 — Docs
- `status.md`: note the content fill-propagation fix + the two new test names.

### Verify
- `cd lib/rust && cargo test -p pathland-render-qt --lib -- --test-threads=1`.
- `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` to confirm the library rows span the full width.

### One decision before I proceed
The spec wording ties the fix to **fill propagation** (FILL child/Spacer → content fills the viewport), which is consistent with the rest of the model and preserves hug-content behavior. If you'd instead prefer the simpler SwiftUI literal ("content always takes the viewport width on the cross axis"), that's a different, more breaking spec change — I recommend the fill-propagation wording. Proceed with fill-propagation on both the spec and renderer?

A vertical ScrollView only expands vertically to allow scrolling. On the horizontal (cross) axis, it shrinks to fit the width of its content unless configured otherwise.
Default Behavior: A ScrollView wrapped around a short Text view will shrink to fit the text unless you apply .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) to the content or use modern container modifiers.

You're right — I had the model backwards. SwiftUI's `ScrollView` is **not** greedy on both axes: it only expands on its **scroll axis**; on the cross axis it **shrinks to fit content** unless the content is told to fill (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`). The current spec ("layout-greedy on **both** axes") is wrong, and it's reflected in the shared `greedyFills` model (GTK `layout.rs:93` and Qt both treat `SCROLLVIEW` as both-axes greedy).

## Correct model (to encode in the spec)

| Axis | ScrollView's own size | Content proposal |
|------|----------------------|------------------|
| **Scroll axis** (vertical) | greedy — fills available space | **unbounded** — grows past the viewport (= scrolls) |
| **Cross axis** (horizontal) | **hugs content** by default (shrinks to fit); fill **propagates** — a `FILL`-width content child makes the viewport `FILL`-width | **bounded** to the viewport's cross size |

So full-width scroll content = a `FILL`-width child of the content stack (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`), never by stretching the content or the viewport itself.

## Proposed spec edits

**`spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §ScrollView:**
- Replace *"Layout-greedy on both axes by default"* with *"**Layout-greedy on its scroll axis** — it fills that axis so content can scroll; on the **cross axis** it **hugs its content** (shrinks to fit) unless the content fills. An explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` overrides."*
- Content paragraph: *"measured with an **unbounded proposal on the scroll axis** (may grow beyond the viewport) and a **bounded proposal on the cross axis** (the viewport). **Fill propagation applies on the cross axis**: a `Fill`-width content child (SwiftUI `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`) is itself `Fill` and fills the viewport on that axis; content with no `Fill` child keeps its natural cross size and the viewport shrinks to fit it."*
- Add a note: *"The protocol has no scroll-axis property today — a `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls **vertically** (cross axis = horizontal). Horizontal scrolling is a future extension (an `AXIS` property)."*

**`spec/LAYOUT.md`:**
- "Layout-greedy primitives" table: `SCROLLVIEW` → **"scroll axis"** (not "both").
- Conformance C13/C14: adjust — vertical fills; horizontal hugs/propagates.

## The one thing I need you to decide

Pathland's `SCROLLVIEW` has **no axis property**. Two ways to resolve:

1. **Default to vertical** (recommended): cross axis = horizontal, matching the demo and the existing C14 example ("no vertical scroll"). Horizontal scroll is deferred until an `AXIS` property is added.
2. **Add an `AXIS`/`SCROLL_AXIS` property now** (enum: Vertical=0, Horizontal=1) — more complete, but a protocol change (emitters, all renderers, conformance vectors).

Which do you want? Once that's settled I'll detail the renderer fix (Qt `greedyFills`/`propagatesFill` + `reconcileScrollSize` content-bounded-to-viewport, and the matching GTK change) and the tests.

## Plan: add `SCROLL_AXIS` to `SCROLLVIEW` (protocol-wide)

This is a cross-cutting protocol change (new constructor property → spec, core, both DSLs, and all renderers). Here's the full plan, phased.

### Phase 0 — Protocol + core

**Allocate the property** (first free layout slot):
- `SCROLL_AXIS` = `0x0021`, value type `F32` (numeric enum code, like `CONTENT_MODE`/`SHAPE_KIND`).
- Enum: `Vertical`=0 (default when absent), `Horizontal`=1.

**`pathland-core/constants.rs`**: add `pub const SCROLL_AXIS: u16 = 0x0021;` (no `value_type_for` change — default is already `F32`).

**Spec edits:**
- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §ScrollView — rewrite intro + Content per your correction:
  - *greedy on the **scroll axis** only; on the **cross axis** it hugs content (shrinks to fit) unless the content fills (fill propagation).*
  - *Content measured **unbounded** on the scroll axis (scrolls) and **bounded** to the viewport on the cross axis; a `Fill`-width child (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`) fills the viewport on that axis.*
  - Document `SCROLL_AXIS` (0x0021, enum) and default = vertical.
- `spec/MODIFIERS.md` — property catalog: mark `0x0021` allocated; add `SCROLL_AXIS` to the enum appendix.
- `spec/LAYOUT.md` — "Layout-greedy primitives" table: `SCROLLVIEW` → "scroll axis" (was "both"); adjust C13/C14 conformance wording.
- `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` — add a golden vector for `SCROLL_AXIS` emission (F32 enum bits).

### Phase 1 — DSLs

- **Rust `pathland-view`**: give `ScrollView` a `ScrollViewConfig` (axis) + a `ScrollAxis` enum; emit `SCROLL_AXIS` only when non-default. Keep `ScrollView::new()`/`children(...)` working.
- **Java `pathland-view`**: add `ScrollAxis` enum + `ScrollView.Config.axis(...)`; `render()` emits `SCROLL_AXIS`. (Verify the annotation processor's configurator rule still holds.)

### Phase 2 — Qt renderer (the one we're actively working on)

- `qmlFor(SCROLL)` / `reconcileScrollSize` become axis-aware:
  - store `g.scroll_axis[id]` (default vertical) from `SCROLL_AXIS`.
  - `effectiveFill(ScrollView, axis)` → greedy on its **scroll axis**; on the **cross axis** propagate from the content (add `SCROLLVIEW` to `propagatesFill` for the cross axis).
  - content sizing: **unbounded** on the scroll axis (grow/scroll), **bounded to the viewport** on the cross axis (fill-propagate).
- Keep the existing HUG_CONTENT / fixed-size behavior.

### Phase 3 — GTK renderer (reference parity)

- `layout.rs::greedy_fills`: make `SCROLLVIEW` fill only its scroll axis (read `SCROLL_AXIS`); add `SCROLLVIEW` to `propagates_fill` for the cross axis.
- `GtkScrolledWindow` policy per axis + content sizing mirrors Qt.

### Phase 4 — HTML renderer + TS DOM client

- Server (`pathland-render-html`): axis-aware `overflow` (`overflow-y:auto` vs `overflow-x:auto`) and greedy on the scroll axis only.
- TS DOM client: apply `SCROLL_AXIS` deltas (or inherit from SSR inline style); no full-tree replay.

### Phase 5 — Tests + status.md

- Per crate: Qt (axis: vertical/horizontal greedy + cross-axis hug/fill-propagation + content bounded/unbounded), GTK, HTML.
- Update each `status.md`.

### Key question (scope)
This touches **every** renderer and both DSLs. Do you want me to:
1. **Land it end-to-end** (all phases above), or
2. **Spec + core + DSLs + Qt first**, then GTK/HTML in a follow-up?

I recommend (2) so the demo (Qt) is unblocked and the protocol is stable before touching the other renderers. Also confirm the enum name — `SCROLL_AXIS` with `Vertical`/`Horizontal` (vs SwiftUI's `Axis`/`.vertical`/`.horizontal` naming) — and the ID `0x0021`.

**Phase 0 — Protocol + core**
- Corrected `spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ScrollView`: greedy only on the **scroll axis**; **cross axis hugs content** (shrinks to fit), fill-propagates from a `FILL`-width content child; content **unbounded on the scroll axis**, **bounded to the viewport on the cross axis**. Added `SCROLL_AXIS` `0x0021` (F32 enum: `Vertical`=0 default, `Horizontal`=1).
- `spec/MODIFIERS.md` catalog + enum appendix; `spec/LAYOUT.md` greedy table + C13/C14; `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vector 34a.
- `pathland-core/constants.rs`: `SCROLL_AXIS`.

**Phase 1 — DSLs**
- Rust `pathland-view`: `ScrollAxis` enum, `ScrollView::axis(...)`/`horizontal()`, emits `SCROLL_AXIS` when horizontal (+2 tests).
- Java `pathland-view`: `ScrollAxis` enum, `ScrollView.Config.axis(...)`, `make(Consumer)`, emits `SCROLL_AXIS`; `Properties.SCROLL_AXIS` (+2 tests).

**Phase 2 — Qt renderer**
- Axis-aware `effectiveFill` (scroll axis greedy; cross axis fill-propagates; removed SCROLL from `greedyFills`), `SCROLL_AXIS` stored/applied.
- `reconcileScrollSize`: content **bounded to the viewport on the cross axis** when it fills, natural otherwise; natural on the scroll axis; viewport implicit cross size hugs when the content doesn't fill; re-derived on resize.
- Tests: fills-only-scroll-axis, fill-content-expands-cross-axis (the library fix), horizontal-axis-greedy, fixed-override, alignment, unbounded content, hug-content. Updated the nav test to give its content a `FILL` width (new model).

GTK (`greedy_fills`/`GtkScrolledWindow`) and HTML (+ TS DOM) still use the old both-axis model — gap notes added to their `status.md`. The demo's library should now expand via the Qt fix; run `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` to confirm.

## Objective
- Build comprehensive spec-compliance test coverage + fixes for the Qt renderer (`pathland-render-qt`), driven by the MusicPlayer demo; most recently **add a `SCROLL_AXIS` property to `SCROLLVIEW`** so a vertical ScrollView only greedily fills its scroll axis and hugs its content on the cross axis (fixes library rows not expanding horizontally).

- Spec is authoritative and is **not** CSS flexbox: cross-axis default is **HUG**; only "effectively FILL" children stretch (explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT=FILL`, greedy primitives, or fill propagation). `ALIGNMENT` positions only.

## Root cause

The sidebar is only in the **wide** `SizeThatFits` candidate (`MusicPlayerView.java:187-193`). At mount, the fit slot starts at index 0, which is the **compact** row (thresholds sort ascending: compact=`0`, wide=`1024`). The Qt renderer measures the slot and reports `FIT_CHANGED(1)`, but the Java demo's ring decoder silently drops that event:

`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo/.../RingEventReader.java:60-84` — `decodeOne()` has no `Commands.Event.FIT_CHANGED` case, so it falls through `default -> null`. The emitter never learns the window is ≥1024, stays on the compact candidate, and never materializes `NowPlayingSidebar`.

The same omission exists in `lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo/.../RingEventReader.java:62-80` (so the GTK Java demo has the same latent bug). Both also drop `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED`.

## Plan

1. **Fix the Qt demo reader** — `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo/src/main/java/dev/pathland/demo/qt/RingEventReader.java`
   Add:
   ```java
   case Commands.Event.FIT_CHANGED -> Event.fitChanged(a, f32(b));
   ```
   (wire: `a`=node id, `b`=f32 index bits — matches `FrameCodec`/`events.rs`; `Event.fitIndex()` reads it via `value`).

2. **Mirror in the GTK demo reader** — same one-line case in `lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo/.../RingEventReader.java`.

3. **Tests** — in both `RingEventReaderTest`s:
   - encode `FIT_CHANGED` (category 0x03, command 0x13, `a`=slot id, `b`=float bits of `1.0`) and assert `isFitChanged()`, `target()`, and `fitIndex() == 1`;
   - (optional) add a `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` decode test.

4. **Safety-net renderer test** — add a Qt layout test for the wide-row ordering (`HStack[filling ZStack, fixed 280 child]`) to prove the fixed sidebar keeps its width when a fill sibling precedes it (existing coverage is fixed-then-fill).

5. **Verify**
   - `mvn -pl pathland-qt-demo,pathland-gtk-demo -am test`
   - `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` → sidebar visible at 1180px, disappears when narrowed below 1024.

Two decisions for you:

1. Should I also add the `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` case to both readers (same dropped-event class; likely affects the seek slider)?
2. Apply the GTK-demo fix too, or keep this change Qt-only?
Both

## Root cause

The volume slider lives in the player bar's **nested** `SizeThatFits` wide cluster (`PlayerControls.java:98-123`). At mount only the compact cluster exists; the slider is created when the renderer reports `FIT_CHANGED` and the emitter reconciles that slot.

The Java emitter adds `BINDING_ID` (the renderer's event gate) **only in `emitNode`** (`Emitter.java:520`), which runs for the initial full emission. Nodes created later go through `emitSubtreeInto` (`:900`) and matched nodes through `reconcileNode` (`:830`) — neither adds it. So the volume slider has no `BINDING_ID`, the Qt/GTK bridge's `fire()` gate (`bridge.cpp:10-13`) drops every `VALUE_CHANGED`, and the slider moves natively while the app never sees it — audio stays unchanged. The seek slider is created at mount (so it is gated and works); the Rust DSL already sets `BINDING_ID` in `mark_binding` (`pathland-view/src/lib.rs:1399`), so only the Java emitter has the hole.

## Plan

1. **Fix the emitter** (`lib/java/pathland-view/.../emit/Emitter.java`)
   - Extract the existing ring-sink gate into `ensureBindingId(PathlandNode node)`:
     ```java
     if (ringSink() && (node.textInput != null || node.valueInput != null || node.dateInput != null))
         node.properties.computeIfAbsent(Properties.BINDING_ID, k -> node.id);
     ```
   - Call it from `emitNode`, `emitSubtreeInto` (before the property loop), and `reconcileNode` (before the property diff). This covers controls created/updated by any structural reconcile (not just volume — also TextFields/date pickers materialized via a fit slot or conditional).

2. **Make the gate testable without the dylib** (small, optional but recommended)
   - `OpcodeSink`: add `default boolean requiresBindingId() { return false; }`.
   - `RingOpcodeSink`: override to `true`; `Emitter.ringSink()` delegates to `sink.requiresBindingId()`.

3. **Regression test** (`SizeThatFitsTest` or a new `BindingGateTest`)
   - Use a `FrameOpcodeSink` subclass returning `requiresBindingId() == true`.
   - Mount `SizeThatFits(Fit.of(compactText), Fit.of(Slider(...bound...), 100))`, fire `fitInputs` → index 1, then assert the new `SLIDER` node's frame carries `SET_PROPERTY(BINDING_ID)`.
   - Add a second case for a `TextField` created the same way, and assert a default frame sink still omits it (SSR unchanged).

4. **Docs**: note in `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` that gated controls created during structural reconciles carry `BINDING_ID` (event round-trip).

5. **Verify**
   - `mvn -pl pathland-view -o test` + `mvn -pl pathland-demo-views -o test`.
   - `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` → drag volume: audio changes; no Rust changes needed (GTK demo fixed by the shared emitter).

One confirmation before I implement: in the Qt demo, does the volume slider **appear and its thumb move** while the audio stays the same? If instead the slider never appears, that's a separate `PlayerBar`-width/threshold issue (the nested cluster needs ≥700pt) and I'd investigate the bar's fill distribution too.
Yes. It appears and I can move the thumb, but the volume stays the same

Confirmed — that symptom is exactly the missing event gate: the Qt slider updates its own thumb, but the renderer drops `VALUE_CHANGED` because the node was created during a reconcile and never received `BINDING_ID`.

## Final plan

### 1. Fix the Java emitter (root cause)
`lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/dev/pathland/view/emit/Emitter.java`

- Extract the existing inline gate from `emitNode` (`:515-522`) into:
  ```java
  private void ensureBindingId(PathlandNode node) {
      if (ringSink() && (node.textInput != null || node.valueInput != null || node.dateInput != null))
          node.properties.computeIfAbsent(Properties.BINDING_ID, k -> node.id);
  }
  ```
- Call `ensureBindingId(...)` from **all three** emission paths:
  - `emitNode` (mount — replaces the inline block),
  - `emitSubtreeInto` (`:899`, before the property loop) — **the volume slider's path**,
  - `reconcileNode` (`:830`, before the property diff) — covers a node that gains a binding.
- This also fixes any TextField/date picker materialized by a fit slot or conditional, not just volume.

### 2. Make the gate testable without the native lib (recommended, small)
- `OpcodeSink`: add `default boolean requiresBindingId() { return false; }`.
- `RingOpcodeSink`: override to `true`.
- `Emitter.ringSink()` → `sink.requiresBindingId()` (removes the `instanceof` coupling).

### 3. Regression tests
`lib/java/pathland-view/src/test/.../SizeThatFitsTest.java` (or a new `BindingGateTest`):
- Use a `FrameOpcodeSink` subclass returning `requiresBindingId() == true`.
- Mount `SizeThatFits(Fit.of(Text…), Fit.of(Slider(value(vol).in(0,1)), 100))`, fire the slot's fit input → index 1, assert the newly created `SLIDER` frame contains `SET_PROPERTY(BINDING_ID)`.
- Same assertion for a `TextField` created via a reconcile.
- Assert a plain `FrameOpcodeSink` still omits `BINDING_ID` (SSR payload unchanged).

### 4. Docs
- Note in `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`: gated controls created during structural reconciles carry `BINDING_ID`, so their raw inputs round-trip.

### 5. Verify
- `cd lib/java && mvn -pl pathland-view -o test`
- `mvn -pl pathland-demo-views -o test`
- `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`: drag the volume slider → audio level changes.
- Qt suite unaffected (no Rust changes: the Rust DSL already sets `BINDING_ID` in `mark_binding`; the GTK Java demo is fixed by the shared emitter).

No changes to the protocol, spec, or Qt renderer are needed. Shall I proceed?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the Java + Qt Quick desktop demo: the shared MusicPlayerView (an Apple
# Music-style player with app-driven media) under the Qt renderer, over the
# libpathland_core shared ring.
#
# macOS must run Qt on the main thread (-XstartOnFirstThread); Linux needs no flag.
set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib.sh"

# Point the Qt renderer's build script at Homebrew's qmake if it isn't on PATH.
if command -v qmake6 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  :
elif [ -x /opt/homebrew/opt/qtbase/bin/qmake ]; then
  export QMAKE=/opt/homebrew/opt/qtbase/bin/qmake
fi

build_qt_dylibs
java_install

case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin)  EXT=".dylib"; MAINTHREAD="-XstartOnFirstThread" ;;
  Linux)   EXT=".so";    MAINTHREAD="" ;;
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) EXT=".dll"; MAINTHREAD="" ;;
  *) echo "unsupported OS: $(uname -s)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

CPFILE="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$CPFILE"' EXIT
mvn -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile="$CPFILE"
CP="target/classes:$(cat "$CPFILE")"

exec java $MAINTHREAD \
  -Dpathland.core.lib="$ROOT/lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_core$EXT" \

content.text:
## Root cause

The Qt renderer's diff re-sends a node's **entire property set** (preceded by `RESET_NODE`) whenever *any* property changes (`renderer.rs:147-188`). A volume drag changes `MEDIA_VOLUME` on the `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`, so that same frame re-sends the controller's other properties too — including:

- `MEDIA_SOURCE` → `applyStringProperty` unconditionally calls `player->setProperty("source", …)`, which reloads the stream from 0;
- `MEDIA_POSITION` (bound to the app's seek command, usually `0`) → `setPosition(0)` seeks back to the start.

So every volume change restarts playback. The GTK renderer already guards both cases (`lib.rs:708-748`: reuse the player when `player.source == resolved`, and seek only when the `MEDIA_POSITION` target **changes**); the Qt renderer lacks those guards.

## Plan

### 1. Qt renderer — make media commands idempotent (`qt_layer.cpp`)
- Add per-controller state next to `media_play_state` (`:344`):
  - `std::unordered_map<uint32_t, QString> media_source;` (last applied resolved URL),
  - `std::unordered_map<uint32_t, float> media_position;` (last applied seek command).
- `PL_PROP_MEDIA_SOURCE` (`:2299`): resolve the asset; if it equals the stored value, **skip** (no `setProperty("source")`, no play re-apply). Otherwise store it, set the source, and re-apply the retained play state (real track change still starts playback).
- `PL_PROP_MEDIA_POSITION` (`:2234`): read the target; if it equals the last applied command, **skip** `setPosition`; otherwise store + seek.
- `deleteNode` (`:2586`): erase both maps (and `media_play_state`) for the id so an id-reused controller starts clean.
- `pathland_qt_layer_reset` (`:~2962`): clear both maps.

### 2. Test hooks (`ffi.rs` + `qt_layer.cpp`)
- Add counters `media_source_sets[id]` / `media_seeks[id]`, exposed as `pathland_qt_layer_media_source_sets(id)` / `pathland_qt_layer_media_seeks(id)` (assert in the extern block).
- New test `media_transport_is_idempotent_across_full_property_resend`:
  1. create `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`, set source + position(0) + volume(0.5) + play → source sets = 1, seeks = 1;
  2. re-apply the **whole property set** with only the volume changed (0.8) — the renderer's re-send shape → still source sets = 1, seeks = 1 (no restart);
  3. a genuinely different source / position → counters increment.
  - Verify the test **fails** with the guards removed.

### 3. Docs
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md` (media section, `:216-219`): note that source reload and seek are applied only on change, so a full property re-send (e.g. a volume update) does not restart playback.

### 4. Verify
- `cd lib/rust && cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (all tests).
- `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`: drag the volume during playback — audio level changes, position continues (no restart); next/prev still restart on the new source as intended.

No protocol/spec/emitter changes. The GTK renderer already behaves correctly; the web path is unaffected (it receives only the changed property from the emitter).

I recommend the localized media-idempotence guard (mirrors GTK, lowest risk) over changing the general diff/reset behavior. Shall I implement it?

## 4. Events

The media event family reports a **controller's** playback state back to the
application. `A` = the **controller** node id (never a surface id).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags |
|---------|-------|----|----|----|-------|
| `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` | `0x0F` | controller id | playing (0/1) | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` | `0x10` | controller id | seconds (f32) | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_ENDED` | `0x11` | controller id | 0 | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` | `0x12` | controller id | volume (f32, 0..1) | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` | `0x14` | controller id | seconds (f32) | 0 | — |

The full event table, encoding, and cadence live in
[EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#media).

### 4.1 Guards

- Media events flow **by virtue of the controller** — no `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit,
  mirroring `VALUE_CHANGED`.
- They flow **only when the application bound the matching control property on
  the controller**: `PLAYBACK_STATE` gates `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` and
  `MEDIA_ENDED`; `MEDIA_POSITION` gates `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` and
  `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED`; `MEDIA_VOLUME` gates `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED`. An
  unbound controller reports nothing (so a purely renderer-native playback stays
  silent).
- The gates are evaluated **on the controller**, not on the surface: binding a
  transport property on a surface has no effect.

### 4.2 Commands vs. reports (MUST)

`MEDIA_POSITION` / `MEDIA_VOLUME` are **commands**; `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` /
`MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` are **reports**. An application
MUST NOT bind a command property to the signal its matching report updates — that
echoes every report back as a command. Bind the command to a

    candidate 1: NowPlayingBar   → controls controller 9
```

(For video the same shape holds with a `VIDEO` surface inside each candidate,

On a band crossing the application swaps the slot's child: the renderer
`DELETE_NODE`s the outgoing subtree and `CREATE_NODE`s the incoming one. What
MUST hold:

1. **Playback continues.** The renderer MUST NOT stop, restart, re-load, or
   re-seek the controller's playback because a view was destroyed/created. Its
   current position, play state, volume, mute, loop, and rate are preserved.
2. **The event target is stable.** Reports continue to carry the controller id
   (9), so the application's bindings never see a "moving target" across a swap.
3. **Zero opcodes for the controller.** The swap emits `TREE` deltas for the
   swapped views only; the controller emits nothing (nothing changed about it).
4. **Nothing is keyed by the swapped node.** The renderer MUST NOT key playback
   by any node other than the controller id. Playback is keyed **by controller
   id** — one playback per controller, for the life of the controller node.

A controller that is itself destroyed (its `DELETE_NODE`) releases its playback.
Creating a new controller starts a new playback.

## 2. The controller — `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30

### 2.1 Protocol

- A **leaf** node: it has no children. A `VIDEO` surface references it by id;
  it is not that surface's child.
- It carries the media resource and the transport properties (§2.3).
- It is created, updated, and deleted like any other node (`TREE` `CREATE_NODE` /
  `DELETE_NODE`), so it participates in the ordinary structural diff, in a
  full-snapshot (`META::RESYNC`), and in proxy-id remapping
  ([PROXY.md](./PROXY.md)) with no media-specific machinery.
- A controller is **not** a media surface and never renders a visual.

### 2.2 Layout (MUST)

A `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` is **layout-transparent**, like `COMMENT` and the
`PROXY_VIEW` passthrough ([LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md)):

- It renders **no native element**.
- It occupies **no space**: it is excluded from its parent's allocation and
  contributes **no spacing** in a stack or grid (it is not a slot).
- It imposes no alignment, sizing, or content-mode behavior.

Its position in the tree is therefore semantically irrelevant; applications place
it for **lifetime stability**, not for layout.

### 2.3 Transport properties

| Property | Id | Type | Meaning |
|----------|----|------|---------|
| `MEDIA_SOURCE` | `0x103B` | STRING (arena ref) | The media resource: a resource name, file path, or absolute URL. An **asset reference**, never embedded in the opcode stream. Changing it re-loads the resource (and resets position to 0 unless a `MEDIA_POSITION` is applied in the same batch). |
| `PLAYBACK_STATE` | `0x1035` | U32 (0 pause, 1 play) | Transport **command**: play/pause. |
| `MEDIA_POSITION` | `0x1036` | F32 (seconds) | Seek **command**. A change seeks; it is **not** a continuous position feed (see §4.3). |
| `MEDIA_VOLUME` | `0x1037` | F32 (0..1) | Volume **command**. |
| `MEDIA_MUTED` | `0x103C` | U8 (0/1) | Mute **command**. Independent of `MEDIA_VOLUME` (the volume value is preserved). |
| `MEDIA_LOOP` | `0x103D` | U8 (0/1) | Loop the resource on end. When set, `MEDIA_ENDED` is still reported, and playback continues from 0. |
| `MEDIA_RATE` | `0x103E` | F32 | Playback rate (1.0 = normal). 0 is equivalent to pause. |

- A controller with **no** `MEDIA_SOURCE` is valid: it is idle and reports
  nothing. The renderer MUST NOT create a playback for it.
- `PLAYBACK_STATE`, `MEDIA_POSITION`, `MEDIA_VOLUME`, `MEDIA_MUTED`,
  `MEDIA_LOOP`, and `MEDIA_RATE` are **commands** the application writes.
  `MEDIA_SOURCE` is the resource binding.

### 2.4 Independence from video surfaces (MUST)

A controller's playback is **independent of its video surfaces**:

- Attaching a surface does **not** start, stop, seek, or re-load playback.
- Detaching (or destroying) a surface does **not** stop playback. A controller
  with **zero** surfaces is valid and keeps playing — the application decides
  when to pause (a `PLAYBACK_STATE` write).
- One controller = **one** playback. Two surfaces referencing the same
  controller share that single playback: a transport command from either affects
  both, and the reports describe both.

---

## 3. The video surface — `VIDEO` 0x0A

`VIDEO` is the **only** media view. It names its controller with
`MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (0x103A, U32 — the controller node id) and renders that
playback's video output in its own box, fitted per `CONTENT_MODE` (`Fit`/`Fill`).
With no children it presents renderer-native video controls; with children (a
`VideoStyle`) the children are the control UI.

- **Audio has no surface.** The removed `AUDIO` component is not replaced: an
  audio playback is rendered by **nothing** in the protocol — the application's
  own views are the entire control surface (§1).
- **Multiplicity**: any number of `VIDEO` surfaces may reference one controller
  (the same playback shown in two places), and any number of controllers may
  coexist.
- **A surface carries no source.** `VIDEO_SOURCE` (0x1034) — like `AUDIO_SOURCE`

`MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` are **reports**. An application
MUST NOT bind a command property to the signal its matching report updates — that
echoes every report back as a command. Bind the command to a
**user-interaction-only** signal and route the report to a separate display
signal.

### 4.3 Renderer echo guard (MUST)

A renderer MUST NOT act on a command write that matches the value it last

interacting. A `MEDIA_POSITION` write within `0.25 s` of the last
`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` must not seek; a `MEDIA_VOLUME` write within `0.01` of the
last `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` must not re-apply. The guard is **per controller**.

content.text:
## Root cause

On natural end the Qt QML reports the stop as a play-state change:

`qt_layer.cpp` (`PL_COMP_MEDIA_CONTROLLER`, ~`:564`):
```qml
onPlaybackStateChanged: bridge.mediaPlayState(%1, playbackState === MediaPlayer.PlayingState)
```

That report goes into the **same** `playing` signal the app uses as the `PLAYBACK_STATE` command (`MediaController.onPlayStateChanged` → `c.playing().set(false)`), so at `EndOfMedia` the app's command flips to pause. `MEDIA_ENDED` then advances the track; the new source loads, and the retained play state is now **0**, so Qt starts the next track paused.

The other renderers don't report app-driven play-state changes:
- **DOM**: play/pause are reported only when the media has **native controls** (`apply.ts:1438-1455`); app-driven audio never reports. On `MEDIA_SOURCE` it explicitly calls `resumeIfPlaying` (`apply.ts:851-859`).
- **GTK**: reports `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` only on **error** (`lib.rs:822`).

Qt is the only one echoing the end/stop, and it has no native-controls path (`VIDEO` → `Item { VideoOutput }`), so the echo is never user-driven.

## Plan (recommended)

### 1. Qt renderer: stop echoing app-driven play state
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/qt_layer.cpp` (MediaPlayer QML in `PL_COMP_MEDIA_CONTROLLER`):
- Remove `onPlaybackStateChanged: bridge.mediaPlayState(...)`.
- Optionally report only genuine failures, matching GTK:
  ```qml
  onMediaStatusChanged: {
      if (mediaStatus === MediaPlayer.EndOfMedia) bridge.mediaEnded(%1)
      else if (mediaStatus === MediaPlayer.InvalidMedia) bridge.mediaPlayState(%1, false)
  }
  ```
- Keep the existing source-change behavior: it re-applies the retained `PLAYBACK_STATE` (the app's command), so the next track starts playing (this is the Qt equivalent of the DOM's `resumeIfPlaying`). Our earlier idempotence guard ensures this only happens on a real source change.

### 2. Docs
- `pathland-render-qt/status.md` media section: `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` is not echoed for app-driven playback (no native controls); it is reported only on media error — matching the DOM client (native-controls-only) and GTK (error-only). Note the end→next transition keeps the app's play command.

### 3. Tests
- Add a demo-level test (`MusicPlayerViewTest`) for the contract: tap play (command = true), dispatch `MEDIA_ENDED`, assert the next track's `MEDIA_SOURCE` is emitted and the app does **not** emit `PLAYBACK_STATE=0`; i.e. `ended()` advances without pausing.
- The actual QML line is only observable with a live media backend, so verify manually: play a track to the end → the next track starts playing, position advances, icon stays on "pause".
- Existing `decode_maps_media_reports` still covers the event plumbing.

### 4. Verify
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (no Rust logic change; the QML is compiled into the dylib).
- `mvn -pl pathland-demo-views -o test`.
- `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`: let a track end → next track continues playing.

## Optional framework hardening (your call)
The Java `MediaController` routes `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` into the **command** `playing` signal, which spec/MEDIA.md §4.2 says not to do. A spec-correct follow-up would add a separate `playingReport()` signal (like `time`/`volumeReport`) and route `onPlayStateChanged` there, with a test that a play-state report never emits `PLAYBACK_STATE`. That would make any renderer's play-state report harmless, but it's a public-API behavior change and not needed for the Qt fix.

Want just the Qt fix, or the Qt fix **plus** the `MediaController` report/command separation?
Both

  - `mediaInputs.get(id).onPlayStateChanged(false)`;

- `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt`
- `mvn -pl pathland-view,pathland-demo-views,pathland-server-core -o test`

### Tradeoff
Part B changes `MediaController` semantics: a renderer-reported play/pause now updates `playingReport()` instead of `playing()`. Apps that displayed the command will still see their own intent (correct for app-driven media); apps displaying actual state should bind `playingReport()`. This is exactly what spec/MEDIA.md §4.2 requires. The Rust `MediaController` doesn't route play-state reports at all, so no equivalent change is needed.

  before the source is re-applied when the source lands.

content.text:
Done — both fixes are in.

**Qt renderer** (`qt_layer.cpp`, controller QML)
- Removed `onPlaybackStateChanged: bridge.mediaPlayState(...)`; the natural-end stop is no longer echoed back.
- Kept a play-state report **only** for `InvalidMedia` (matching GTK's error-only behavior).
- On a real source change the retained `PLAYBACK_STATE` is re-applied, so the next track starts playing (Qt's equivalent of the DOM's `resumeIfPlaying`).

**Framework** (`MediaController` / `Emitter`)
- Added the `playingReport()` report feed (`playingReport(WritableSignal<Boolean>)` + getter), like `time`/`volumeReport`.
- `Emitter.applyController` now routes `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` → `playingReport()`, never the `playing()` command — so no renderer can clobber the app's play intent (spec/MEDIA.md §4.2).
- Updated the class Javadoc and the command/report docs.

**Tests**
- `MediaControllerTest.playStateReportDoesNotEchoBackAsAPlaybackCommand` — verified it **fails** with the old routing (`PLAYBACK_STATE` frame emitted) and passes now.
- `MusicPlayerViewTest.endedAdvancesWithoutPausing` — seeds `playing=true`, dispatches `MEDIA_ENDED`, and asserts the next track's `MEDIA_SOURCE` is emitted with **no** `PLAYBACK_STATE` pause (scans the whole multi-frame delta).
- `status.md` updated for both the Qt report policy and the Java report feeds.

**Verified:** `pathland-view` 163, `pathland-demo-views` 38, `pathland-server-core` 62, `pathland-render-html` 11, Qt suite 87 — all pass; full Java reactor install succeeds. Re-run `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`: a track will now advance and keep playing when it ends.

content.text:
The failure is a wrong package name: `qml6-module-qtquick-window2` is the **Qt5** module name. On Ubuntu 24.04 (`ubuntu-latest`) the Qt6 package is `qml6-module-qtquick-window`. The QML runtime also needs `qml6-module-qtquick-layouts` (every stack is a `RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout`), which isn't currently listed — noble's `qt6-declarative-dev` pulls the C++ libs but not the QML runtime modules.

## Plan

### 1. Fix `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Qt install step)
Replace the package list with:
```yaml
sudo apt-get install -y \
  qt6-base-dev \
  qt6-declarative-dev \
  qt6-multimedia-dev \
  qml6-module-qtquick \
  qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
  qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
  qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
  qml6-module-qtquick-window \
  qml6-module-qtmultimedia
```
- `qml6-module-qtquick-window2` → `qml6-module-qtquick-window` (the actual failure).
- Add `qml6-module-qtquick-layouts` for `import QtQuick.Layouts` (stacks/grid).
- Keep `templates` (Controls dependency) and `window` (Controls/Popup internals).
- Update the comment to say the `qml6-module-*` runtime modules (Quick, Layouts, Controls, Templates, Window, Multimedia) are required because the offscreen tests instantiate QML via `QQmlComponent`.

### 2. Validate before pushing
Docker is available; verify the exact package names against a clean noble image:
```bash
docker run --rm ubuntu:24.04 bash -c 'apt-get update -qq && \
  apt-get install -y --simulate qt6-base-dev qt6-declarative-dev qt6-multimedia-dev \
  qml6-module-qtquick qml6-module-qtquick-layouts qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
  qml6-module-qtquick-templates qml6-module-qtquick-window qml6-module-qtmultimedia'
```
(`--simulate` resolves the graph without installing.)

### 3. Confirm no other references
`grep -rn "qml6-module"` shows only `ci.yml` — no other workflow/script needs the rename.

### 4. Commit
`ci(rust): fix Qt6 QML module names on noble` — then push and let the workflow run.

No code/spec changes; this is purely the CI dependency list. Note the Java job doesn't install Qt libs (its tests don't load Qt), so no change there.

content.text:
The CI got past the package install and now fails in the Qt crate's build script. Three separate Linux/Qt‑6.4 issues are stacked up:

## Root causes

1. **`build.rs:67` panics when qmake is a bare PATH name.**
   `qmake_bin()` falls back to `PathBuf::from("qmake6")` on Linux. Then `qmake.parent()` is `Some("")`, and `qt_bin.parent()` is `None` → `expect("qmake bin has a prefix")`. On noble, `qmake6` is `/usr/bin/qmake6`, and `moc` lives in `QT_INSTALL_LIBEXECS=/usr/lib/qt6/libexec`, not next to qmake.

2. **The Qt Quick Layouts private header isn't available.**
   `qt_layer.cpp` includes `<QtQuickLayouts/private/qquicklayout_p.h>`. On noble that's in **`qt6-declarative-private-dev`** (not installed by CI), and the versioned include dirs aren't added: it needs `-I…/qt6/QtQuickLayouts/6.4.2` and `-I…/qt6/QtQuick/6.4.2/QtQuick` etc. The build script only adds the flat `QtQuickLayouts/private/` dirs on macOS.

3. **Qt 6.4 compatibility.** Ubuntu 24.04 ships Qt 6.4.2, which lacks `QStyleHints::colorScheme()`, `Qt::ColorScheme`, and `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged` (added in 6.5) — `qt_layer.cpp` uses all three.

I verified all of this in a clean `ubuntu:24.04` container: moc works, and the two `.cpp` files compile with the extra include dirs **except** the three `colorScheme` errors.

## Plan

### 1. `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/build.rs`
- Make moc discovery tolerant of a bare qmake:
  - Add `qmake_query_opt()` (returns `Option`, no panic).
  - `find_moc`: only use `qmake.parent()` when non-empty; then query `QT_INSTALL_LIBEXECS` and `QT_INSTALL_BINS` (works for bare `qmake6`) and try `<dir>/moc`/`<dir>/moc6`; keep the static fallbacks.
- Add Linux/Qt include dirs generically (after `build.include(&headers)`):
  - For each module in `modules`: `{headers}/{Module}`, and for each version subdir `{headers}/{Module}/{v}` and `{headers}/{Module}/{v}/{Module}`.
  - This resolves `<QtQuickLayouts/private/…>` and the nested `<private/qquickitem_p.h>` / `<QPointer>` chain on Debian/Ubuntu; harmless on macOS.

### 2. `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`
- Guard the color-scheme code:
  ```cpp
  #if QT_VERSION >= QT_VERSION_CHECK(6, 5, 0)
      const bool dark = g.app->styleHints()->colorScheme() == Qt::ColorScheme::Dark;
  #else

content.text:
Fixed and committed as `d85aec3e`. The CI failure was the first of four Linux/Qt‑6.4 issues; I validated the whole chain in a clean Ubuntu 24.04 container.

**Build (`build.rs`)**
- `moc` is now found via `qmake -query QT_INSTALL_LIBEXECS/BINS` (a bare `qmake6` has no parent dir) — fixes the `qmake bin has a prefix` panic.
- Added Debian/Ubuntu module + versioned private include dirs (for `QtQuickLayouts/private/qquicklayout_p.h`).
- `-F{libs}` is passed before compiling (macOS framework includes).
- The static archive is compiled/emitted **before** the Qt link libs so Linux's `--as-needed` doesn't drop them (undefined `QMetaTypeInterfaceWrapper` at link).

**Runtime (`qt_layer.cpp`)**
- `QGuiApplication` now receives `argc` **by reference** — the by-value local dangled and made `QCoreApplication::arguments()` segfault on Linux/Qt 6.4.
- Color scheme falls back to the palette on Qt < 6.5 (no `QStyleHints::colorScheme`).

**Tests (`ffi.rs`)**
- `c_char` buffers (it's `u8` on aarch64 Linux).

**CI**
- Added `qt6-declarative-private-dev` and `qml6-module-qtqml`, `-models`, `-workerscript` (the QML engine requires WorkerScript); GStreamer was already installed.

Verified: Ubuntu 24.04/Qt 6.4.2 (arm64) **87/87** tests, serial and parallel; macOS **87/87**. Working tree clean.

`pathland-render-core::HostNode` gained `lists` (LIST-typed props such as `FIT_QUERY`) and `date` (`DATE_PICKER`), but four GTK test fixtures still used the old literal. Added `lists: HashMap::new(), date: None` to the three helpers in `layout.rs` and the one in `lib.rs`.
